  • The devices of included topologies, read only, unless you combine them.
  • The annotations of the config, which the Inspector shows with nothing selected. Publishing does not write them.

An import uses the Default layout: the devices in rows on a grid, and the switches below them. It sets no subnet or gateway, because a config has none. A warning names every other change (see What an import keeps).

docs.title: Upload a Builder document
docs.text:
A Builder document is the file that Download > Builder JSON or Builder YAML saves (see Builder JSON and YAML). Upload opens one as a new draft:

  1. On the drafts page or in the editor toolbar, click Upload.
  2. Keep Source set to File.
  3. In Builder document file, choose the file, for example pump-station.builder.json.
  4. Click Upload. The new draft has the name in the document.

Source has three other choices:

  • Paste text takes the document as text.
  • Published diagram opens the draft of a published diagram.
  • Legacy Builder diagram or Topology converts a diagram from the legacy Builder (see Legacy Builder).

Upload refuses a config, a template file, a layer set file, a file that is not JSON or YAML, and a file over 5 MiB. The dialog gives the reason (see Uploading a Builder document).

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
1. Open the draft.
  2. Click Download.
  3. Click a format. The browser saves the file.
  4. Click Close.
Button What the file holds Open it with Builder JSON The whole diagram, with its icons and templates Upload Builder YAML The same, as YAML Upload Topology YAML The Topology config that Publish would write phenix config create, or Import PNG A picture of the whole diagram An image viewer SVG The same picture, as SVG A web browser draw.io The diagram, in the draw.io format draw.io Gephi (GEXF) The devices, networks and connections, in the GEXF format Gephi Builder package The diagram with the configs and icons that you tick Upload

The file name is the diagram name in lower case with hyphens, for example riverside-water.png (see Download formats).

For Topology YAML, when the diagram cannot be published yet, the dialog saves the file and lists each reason. Thus the download is a quick way to see what blocks publishing (see Topology YAML). phenix config create stores this file as a topology without its diagram. To store both, publish the draft (see Publishing).

PNG and SVG draw the whole diagram, with the background of the theme in use (see PNG and SVG). Builder cannot open a draw.io or GEXF file (see draw.io and Gephi (GEXF)).

docs.title: Move a diagram with a Builder package
docs.text:
Another phēnix server may not have the scenarios, included topologies, custom icons and disk images that a diagram names. A Builder package is one JSON or YAML file. It holds the diagram, the configs and icons that you tick, and a list of everything that the diagram needs.

To download a package:

  1. Click Download.
  2. Under Builder package, tick Scenario configs, Included topologies, Custom icons or Disk-image requirements.
  3. In Package format, select JSON or YAML.
  4. Click Builder package.

To upload a package on the other server:

  1. Click Upload.
  2. In Builder document file, choose the package file.
  3. Click Upload. The dialog lists each item that the diagram needs as Present, Missing, Different or Not checked.
  4. For each missing config to create, tick Create on this server. Builder never replaces a config that the server has.
  5. Click Continue to editor. Builder creates the ticked configs, adds the missing icons, and opens the diagram as a new draft.

A package never holds disk images, apps or files. It lists them by name (see Moving a diagram with a Builder package).

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text:
• A layer set file holds one layer set of the library. You download and upload it on the Layers tab of the drafts page. See Layer set files.
  • phenix config create refuses a Builder document, a template file, a package and a layer set file, and skips them in a directory. See Builder documents and phenix config create.
  • A topology in a repository can name its Builder file in its builder-doc annotation, and its diagram then opens from the file. See A Builder file beside a topology.
  • A Builder document records who made the diagram and who saved it last. See Who made and last saved a diagram.

docs.title: More detail
docs.text:
• Import, Upload and Download: details: every rule, option and message.
  • File formats.
  • Legacy Builder: converting diagrams of the old editor.

docs.title: Legacy Builder
docs.text: Earlier phēnix releases had a different graphical editor, also named Builder, built on mxGraph. It opened at /builder in a new browser tab. This release does not have the legacy Builder.

docs.title: What changed
docs.text:
Legacy Builder Builder Where phēnix keeps a diagram XML in the builder-xml annotation of the topology A draft on the phēnix server. Publish stores the diagram and names it in the builder-doc annotation What writes the topology Save to phēnix Publish (see Publishing) A line between two devices A direct connection A switch for each network. Converting adds the missing switch Experiment variables Placeholders such as $DEFAULT_MEMORY The values, in each node Tag on the Configs page builder legacy builder REST routes POST /builder/save, /api/v1/builder/topologies, /api/v1/experiments/builder Removed (see REST API)

Topologies from the legacy Builder still run, because phēnix never read the diagram to run an experiment. Convert a diagram only to edit it as a diagram.

On the Configs page, the viewer and Edit show the annotation as builder-xml: <SNIPPED>. phēnix keeps the diagram while that line does not change. If you delete the line, phēnix deletes the diagram.

docs.title: Converting a stored topology
docs.text:
Import converts the diagram of a stored topology that has builder-xml and no builder-doc:

  1. In the phēnix navigation bar, click Builder.
  2. Click Import.
  3. Keep Stored config and the Source kind Topology.
  4. In Source name, choose the topology. Its name has the suffix "(legacy Builder diagram)".
  5. Click Import.
  6. If the dialog lists warnings (see Warnings), click Continue to editor.

The editor opens the converted draft. Change the draft as necessary. Then, to replace the legacy diagram:

  1. Click Publish.
  2. In Topology name, enter the name of the topology.
  3. Click Update topology.
  4. Click Update topology again.

The result shows the warning "This diagram replaced the legacy Builder diagram of topology NAME."

The draft uses the nodes of the topology. The old diagram gives only the position of each node, matched by hostname, and the notes and groups.

Nothing changes on the server until you publish. Publishing to the same topology deletes builder-xml, writes builder-doc and keeps the other annotations. The topology then has the tag builder.

On the Configs page, the builder legacy tag and the Import into Builder button of the viewer open the same Import dialog, set to that topology (see Import, Upload and Download).

With the import options, a copy, or a draft that combines the included topologies, publishes a new topology. The legacy topology then keeps its builder-xml.

Only the draft imported from the topology itself can replace its legacy diagram. Other drafts cannot update the topology, such as a draft imported from an experiment of the topology, or an uploaded file. Publish them under a different name.

If the topology or its legacy diagram changes after the import, Publish refuses (see When the source config changed).

When the import cannot read the diagram, the draft has no layout from it (see Warnings). Publishing then deletes builder-xml too, with the warning "The server could not read the legacy Builder diagram of topology NAME. The server removed it."

docs.title: Converting a file
docs.text:
Upload converts a legacy diagram in a file:

  1. On the drafts page or in the editor toolbar, click Upload.
  2. Under Source, choose Legacy Builder diagram or Topology.
  3. In Legacy diagram or Topology file, choose the file.
  4. Click Convert.
  5. If the dialog lists warnings, click Continue to editor.

The editor opens a new draft. Its name is the file name without its last extension.

The file can be up to 5 MiB, and it must be one of these:

  • An XML file from Save to Disk in the legacy Builder. Its root element is mxGraphModel (or a bare root).
  • A Topology config, as YAML or JSON, with the builder-xml annotation, such as one downloaded from the Configs page.

The converter does not read draw.io files (mxfile), or compressed or base64-encoded diagrams. The File and Paste text sources do not convert a legacy diagram. They say "This is possibly a legacy Builder diagram (XML). Select "Legacy Builder diagram or Topology" to convert it."

Upload refuses other files, for example with "Could not convert the legacy diagram. This is not a legacy Builder diagram. A legacy diagram is mxGraph XML, or a Topology config with the builder-xml annotation." A Topology config without the annotation gives "Could not convert the legacy diagram. Topology NAME has no legacy Builder diagram (no builder-xml annotation). Select Import to make a diagram from it."

A diagram without its topology has only the node settings that the diagram holds. A draft converted from a file always publishes a new topology. It cannot update a stored topology, even one with the same name.

Converting a file needs configs get and create. phēnix keeps each ${NAME} in a Topology config file as written (see Importing a config file). If you close the dialog during the conversion, the conversion stops.

docs.title: What is converted
docs.text:
In the legacy diagram In the Builder A device A device. Its settings come from the topology, or from the diagram when there is no topology A router, firewall, desktop or server icon, in any color The router, firewall, desktop or server icon. An external device gets external. Other icons become the icon of the device type A switch The switch of its network, named after the network A VLAN ID on a switch or a line The VLAN alias of the network, when it is a number from 1 to 4094. 0, auto or none give no alias A line from a device to a switch A connection A line between two devices A connection to a switch added for that network, between its devices Text A note A rectangle or container around nodes A group, with its text as the title A placeholder such as $DEFAULT_VCPU Only for a diagram without a topology: the variable of the diagram, else the legacy default (DEFAULT_MEMORY 2048, DEFAULT_VCPU 1, DEFAULT_VM_IMAGE ubuntu.qc2, DEFAULT_ROUTER_IMAGE vyos.qc2). The value stays text, such as vcpus: "1", as the legacy Builder wrote it Positions Doubled, on the 16-pixel grid, with each device centered where its icon was The grid setting Kept

Positions double because a node card is about twice the size of the old icon. Each device shows its type, such as Router or External.

For a topology, the conversion leaves out a node that is in the diagram but not in the topology. It puts a node of the topology that is not in the diagram below the diagram. Each gives a warning.

docs.title: What is left out
docs.text:
• The name of the legacy switch. A switch has the name of its network.
  • The variables of the diagram, after the conversion fills them in, and the schema and device keys of each node.
  • Icon colors and artwork, and the mobile icon.
  • Shapes, fills, strokes, fonts, rotation, shadows, dashes and arrows, and the HTML formatting of labels.
  • Edge labels, waypoints and lines that are not links between a device and a network.
  • Layers (merged into one), whether a cell was hidden, collapsed or locked, and the stacking order.
  • Tooltips, links and inserted images.
  • Shapes without text.
  • Page settings, such as the page size, background and grid size.
  • The parent of a group nested more than 32 deep.

docs.title: Warnings
docs.text:
The dialog lists each warning before it makes the draft. A list of names shows at most 8 names, then the number of the others.

Warning What it means "The Builder could not read the legacy diagram of topology NAME (…). The Builder did not use its layout. The Builder placed the nodes automatically." The converter cannot read the builder-xml of the topology. The draft has the nodes of the topology, on a grid. Publishing deletes the old diagram "1 node of the legacy diagram is not in the topology. The Builder did not import it: …" The topology changed after the last save of its diagram. The draft uses the nodes of the topology "1 node of the topology was not in the legacy diagram. The Builder placed it below the diagram: …" The same, in the other direction "The Builder added a switch for 1 network that had none in the legacy diagram: …" The diagram joined two devices with a line, or did not draw the network "The Builder did not import 1 link whose node has no interface on that network: NODE to NETWORK." A line joins a device to a network that none of its interfaces uses "VLAN ID VALUE of network NAME is not a number from 1 to 4094. The Builder did not import it." The network has no VLAN alias "Network NAME has more than one VLAN ID in the legacy diagram. The Builder kept the first, ID." Its switches or lines gave other IDs "VLAN ID ID occurs on networks A and B. The Builder kept it only for A." Two networks cannot share an alias "The legacy diagram had N layers. The Builder merged them into one layer." All nodes are on one canvas "1 item has settings that the Builder could not read. The Builder did not import it: …" A node in the diagram has damaged settings "1 node has interfaces that the Builder could not read. The Builder did not import these interfaces: …" Only for a diagram without a topology. The node stays, without those interfaces "The Builder renamed node "OLD" to "NEW": a hostname cannot hold spaces." Spaces became hyphens. A network gets the same change, with "a network name cannot hold spaces" "Used the legacy defaults for variables the diagram does not define: $DEFAULT_MEMORY = 2048, …" Check the values in the Inspector "1 placeholder has no value in the diagram. The Builder kept it as text: $NAME." Replace the text in the Inspector before you publish "The Builder did not import 1 line that was not a network link." or "The Builder did not import 1 shape that had no text." See What is left out "The Builder kept text and containers as notes and groups. The Builder did not convert their colors, fonts and other formatting." Given once, when the diagram has text or containers "The diagram has no nodes." The draft is empty

docs.title: Keeping a copy of the old diagram
docs.text: Before you publish, download the topology from the Configs page. The file holds the XML, and Upload can convert it again. To open the old editor, use phēnix 1.0.0 or an earlier release.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text: Publish writes a Topology config from a draft, and optionally an Experiment config with one of the scenarios that the diagram lists. It uses the last saved snapshot, and the server checks that snapshot again before it writes.

docs.title: Before you publish
docs.text:
• Fix the errors, and the warnings that block publishing (see What blocks publishing).
  • Apply or cancel your changes in the Inspector. Publish applies and saves valid changes. Changes that it cannot apply block publishing, and the dialog names them.
  • Check your permissions. Publish is not available in a published diagram, which opens read only, or when your role cannot update configs.

Publish is in the toolbar, in the command palette as Publish…, and on each card of the drafts page.

docs.title: Publish a topology
docs.text:
To update the topology riverside-water from the Riverside Water draft:

  1. Open the draft.
  2. Click Publish.
  3. Under What to publish, keep Topology only.
  4. Below Topology name, click Use riverside-water. The hint says "A topology with this name exists. Publishing updates it." A config name holds only letters, numbers, _, @, . and -.
  5. Read Checks. It says what is ready to publish.
  6. Click Update topology. Builder asks "Replace topology riverside-water?".
  7. Click Update topology again.
  8. Click Close.

docs.title: What the topology holds
docs.text: The Topology config holds the settings of each device, and the network of each connected interface as its vlan. It does not hold the parts that only Builder uses: positions, groups, notes, drawings, colors, line styles, icons, layers and templates. It also does not hold the Subnet and Gateway of a network.

docs.title: What publishing changes
docs.text:
What publishing changes, above the buttons, compares the server with the result of the publish:

  • The configs that Publish creates, updates or does not change.
  • The included topologies that it adds, removes or keeps.
  • The scenarios that get the topology.
  • The disk images that the devices use.
  • With an experiment, the VLAN aliases that change.

docs.title: Create or update
docs.text:
The hint under Topology name says what publishing does with that name, and the button names the action. When a topology with that name exists and this draft cannot update it, the dialog refuses the name (see Publish hints and buttons).

A draft can update a topology in these cases:

  • The draft published the topology.
  • The draft is an import of the stored topology.
  • You opened the draft from the published diagram.
  • The draft is an upload of a Builder document from such a draft.

A copy, a combined import and an import of a config file cannot update the source topology (see Create or update).

You cannot undo an update. phēnix keeps no earlier version of a config. To go back, restore an earlier snapshot in Draft History. Then publish again. An update keeps the other annotations of the topology and adds builder-doc.

docs.title: The result
docs.text: The dialog lists each stage and its result (see Publish results). When a stage fails, the dialog says "Published with failures." or "Publish failed. It wrote no configs." Remove the cause, for example stop a running experiment. Then click Back and publish again with the same names. The stages that are done show skipped, and Publish writes nothing twice.

docs.title: Publish a topology and an experiment
docs.text:
To update riverside-water and create the experiment riverside-lab:

  1. Open the draft.
  2. Click Publish.
  3. Under What to publish, select Topology and an experiment.
  4. Below Topology name, click Use riverside-water.
  5. In Experiment name, enter riverside-lab.
  6. Keep Experiment scenario riverside-water.
  7. Click Update topology and create experiment. Builder asks "Replace topology riverside-water?".
  8. Click Update topology and create experiment again.
  9. Click Close.

Publish writes the VLAN alias of each network to vlans.aliases of the experiment.

An experiment name follows the config name rule, and it cannot be all. Some servers name each network bridge after its experiment. On these servers, an experiment name has at most 15 characters.

A draft can update only the experiment that it comes from, or that it published. An update runs the configure stage of the apps. Stop the experiment before you update it. An update removes the host pins of devices that are no longer in the topology, with a warning (see Host pins).

docs.title: Scenarios
docs.text: In both modes, Publish adds the topology to the topology annotation of each listed scenario, when the annotation does not name it yet. Experiment scenario selects the scenario of the experiment, or No scenario. Publish refuses when a listed scenario does not exist or your role cannot read it. It also refuses when your role cannot update a listed scenario whose annotation needs the topology (see Scenarios).

docs.title: What blocks publishing
docs.text:
Errors block publishing, for example two devices with one hostname. Five kinds of warnings also block publishing. The draft saves with them, but the Publish dialog lists them as errors:

  • An interface with no network and no VLAN, on a device that is not external.
  • Two interfaces on one network with the same IP address or MAC address.
  • A hostname that phēnix refuses: one character, all, all digits, or phenix on a Windows device.
  • A device setting that stops the experiment:
    • An interface with protocol ospf on a Router or Firewall of OS type vyatta, vyos or linux, with no network.ospf.
    • An ntp-server label that names no interface with an IP address.
  • A device that is not external, with no drive.

Under Checks, the dialog lists the errors first, then the warnings, each with Go to. When the server refuses a publish, the dialog shows its reason and its issues with their codes.

If you copy historian-01, as in the tutorial, Publish lists one error (see Example: Riverside Water expansion).

Tip

Download > Topology YAML saves the topology that Publish would write, and lists every issue that blocks publishing.

docs.title: Publish again
docs.text:
Publish again with the same names after each set of edits. The draft remembers what it published. Two things can stop a second publish:

  • Another draft published the topology.
  • Someone changed the topology outside Builder, for example with phenix config edit.

The hint under Topology name gives the reason. In both cases, edit a draft of the topology as it is now (see Edit a published topology), or publish under another name.

docs.title: When the source config changed
docs.text:
A draft remembers the config that it comes from. Publish refuses the draft under any name when that config changed after Builder made the draft. The dialog shows a warning at the top. To keep your work:

  1. Make a draft of the config as it is now. Click the edit button of the topology on the Configs page, or import it again.
  2. Copy the changed devices from the old draft, and paste them into the new draft.
  3. Connect the pasted devices again. A pasted device keeps its settings but not its connections.

See When the source config changed.

docs.title: Included topologies
docs.text: Riverside Water includes the topology corp-services. The published topology names corp-services and does not copy its devices. A diagram imported with Combine into one new topology publishes the included devices as its own. When the diagram and an included topology use one hostname, Publish refuses (see Included topologies).

docs.title: Edit a published topology
docs.text: On the Configs page, click the tag builder in the row of the topology. Builder opens the draft that published it, or else a draft of the published diagram. Edit as a draft on the Published Diagrams tab opens the same draft (see Editing a published topology).

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text:
• A topology can name a Builder file as its diagram. See A Builder file beside a topology and Publishing to a topology that names a Builder file.
  • A draft imported from a legacy Builder topology replaces its legacy diagram when it publishes to the same topology. See Converting a stored topology.
  • The Scenarios dialog writes Scenario configs to the server at once, and Cancel does not undo them. See Storing scenarios from the Scenarios dialog.

docs.title: More detail
docs.text:
• Publishing: details: every rule, refusal and message.
  • What each task needs: the permissions of publishing.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text: This page holds the tables that the other pages point to, from the save states to the error codes. For the rules behind them, see the details page of each feature.

docs.title: Save states
docs.text:
The save state follows Draft History in the editor toolbar (see How drafts save).

Save state What it means What to do All changes saved The server has all changes. Nothing. Saving changes, Saving 2 changes Builder sends changes. Wait. 2 unsaved changes Changes wait. Wait, or press Ctrl+S (⌘+S on macOS) to run Save now. Offline: 1 change kept on this device. Saving retries automatically. The server cannot be reached, or did not answer in time. This browser keeps the changes. Continue to work. See Working offline. Offline: 2 changes not stored anywhere yet. Keep this tab open. Saving retries automatically. The server cannot be reached, and the browser cannot store the changes. Keep the tab open until the save state says All changes saved. Offline: no unsaved changes The server cannot be reached, and no changes wait. Nothing. 1 change not saved yet. Choose which changes to save. Another tab of this browser has changes to this draft. See Same draft in multiple tabs. Merging your changes with the server version… Someone saved a newer version first. Builder merges it with your changes. Wait. See Draft merging. This draft changed on the server Someone saved a newer version first. Some changes clash, or merging is not available. See Draft merging. Not saved: you chose another tab's changes In another tab of this browser, you chose to save the changes of that tab. This tab does not save its changes. Nothing. Builder keeps the changes of this tab as a new draft. Could not save: someone deleted this draft from the server. Select Download to keep a copy of the diagram. Another user deleted the draft. Click Download (see Downloading). Upload the file to make a new draft. You cannot save changes to this draft Your role no longer includes Builder. Ask an administrator for the Builder permission (see Permissions). Click Download to keep a copy. Could not save your last change. … When you fix the diagram, the Builder saves it again. The server refused the diagram, for example for two devices with one hostname. The message names the error. Fix it (see Checks and warnings). The next change saves the diagram. Could not save your last undo or redo: the server no longer keeps that step. … You went with Undo or Redo to a snapshot that the server deleted, such as an old snapshot past the limit of 50. Nothing. Your next edit saves the diagram as it shows. Could not save. … Remove part of the diagram, or select Download to keep a copy. The diagram is too large for the server to save. The message names the reason. Remove part of the diagram. Or click Download to keep a copy. Could not save your changes. … Saving retries automatically. The server refused the save for a different reason, which the message names. Wait, or click Retry saving.

Retry saving shows when the browser is offline, or when a new try can fix a failed save. It sends the waiting changes immediately.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text:
To see the shortcuts of your platform, click Shortcuts in the header, or press ? outside a text field. "Not in text fields" means that the keys do nothing while focus is in a text field, or in a field of the Inspector. You can give any command other keys (see Customizing shortcuts).

Action Where it works Windows and Linux macOS Command palette Editor and Drafts page, text fields too Ctrl+K ⌘+K Keyboard shortcuts Editor and Drafts page, not in text fields ? ? docs.title: Publish hints and buttons
docs.text:
The hint under Topology name in the Publish diagram dialog says what publishing does with that name, and the button names the action. The hint under Experiment name works the same way (see Create or update).

Hint Button "Publishing creates a new topology." Create topology "A topology with this name exists. Publishing updates it." Update topology "A topology with this name already exists. This diagram cannot update it. …" Builder refuses to publish. Enter another name. "A topology with this name changed after this diagram published it. Publishing would overwrite that change. …" Builder refuses to publish. See Publishing again. "… This diagram replaces its legacy Builder diagram." or "… Builder could not read its legacy Builder diagram. Publishing removes it." Update topology. See Replacing a legacy Builder diagram.

docs.title: Publish results
docs.text:
After a publish, the dialog lists each stage and its result (see The result).

Stage What it is Results document The published copy of the diagram, on the Published Diagrams tab created, or skipped when you publish again and the publication was already complete topology The Topology config created, updated, or skipped when the config already holds this snapshot scenario The topology annotation of each listed scenario updated, with the changed scenarios, or skipped experiment The Experiment config, with Topology and an experiment created, updated or skipped draft The draft records what it published ok, or skipped when you publish again and the publication was already complete

The headline is one of these:

Headline What it means "Published. Every stage succeeded." Every stage succeeded. "Published with failures. …" A stage failed after the server wrote earlier stages. Fix the cause. Click Back. Publish again with the same names. The stages that succeeded show skipped. "Publish failed. It wrote no configs." A stage failed before the server wrote any config. The list shows the failed stage. Fix the cause. Click Back. Publish again.

When the server refuses the publish before it writes anything, the form stays open, and Checks gives the reason after "Could not publish the diagram."

docs.title: Error codes
docs.text:
Each issue that Builder reports has a code: a stable, machine-readable name of the rule that it breaks, such as node.hostname.duplicate. The editor checks and the Builder REST API use the same code for the same rule. Thus a script can act on the code and ignore the message.

A code is lowercase words joined by dots. A word can contain hyphens, such as not-found. The first word names the subject of the rule, such as node, edge (a connection) or layerset (a layer set). A released code keeps its meaning. A new rule gets a new code.

docs.title: Issues
docs.text:
Builder reports each warning and error as an issue:

Field Value code The code of the rule severity error if the issue refuses the request, warning if not message The text that a person sees path The location in the document, such as nodes[3].device.hostname, when the issue is about a part of it nodeId, edgeId, networkId The ID of the node, connection or network, when the issue is about one field The device field, such as spec.network.interfaces.0.vlan, when the issue is about one

The table in Codes gives the default severity of each code. Some issues block only publishing, such as an interface without a VLAN. The editor shows them as warnings on the canvas, because a draft may keep them. The Publish diagram dialog shows them as errors.

An unknown key in an object of the document (document.field.unknown) is an issue at its path. A value of the wrong type is an issue only where the editor also checks the type, such as a number in createdBy (metadata.user.not-text). The server refuses other values of the wrong type, such as a node position that is text, with a message of its own.

docs.title: Errors of the REST API
docs.text:
When a Builder route refuses a request, the JSON body gives the code in code, with message and cause. For a document that does not pass the checks (document.invalid), or a draft that only publishing refuses (publish.blocked), issues lists each warning and error:

{
  "code": "publish.blocked",
  "message": "topology lab cannot be published: interface \"eth1\" of device \"web\" has no VLAN: connect it to a network, or type a VLAN for it",
  "cause": "validating topology projection: interface \"eth1\" of device \"web\" has no VLAN: connect it to a network, or type a VLAN for it",
  "issues": [
    {
      "code": "interface.vlan.missing",
      "severity": "error",
      "message": "interface \"eth1\" of device \"web\" has no VLAN: connect it to a network, or type a VLAN for it",
      "path": "nodes[2].device.spec.network.interfaces[1]",
      "nodeId": "4113dfc0-f4be-57f9-8115-6cecd1f1aea3",
      "field": "spec.network.interfaces.1.vlan"
    }
  ]
}

A refusal about a scenario that a draft lists (publish.scenario.*) names that scenario in metadata.scenario.

These codes have these HTTP statuses. A refusal without a code of its own gets the request.* or server.* code of its status.

Status Codes 400 request.invalid, publish.target.invalid 403 request.forbidden, layerset.read-only 404 request.not-found 405 request.method-not-allowed 409 request.conflict, draft.conflict, draft.snapshot.current, template.item.read-only, publish.topology.exists, publish.topology.missing, publish.topology.not-source, publish.topology.changed, publish.topology.file-mismatch, publish.experiment.exists, publish.experiment.missing, publish.experiment.not-source, publish.experiment.changed 412 request.stale, draft.stale, template.item.stale, layerset.stale 413 request.too-large, draft.limit, layerset.library.full, package.too-large 422 request.unprocessable, document.invalid, publish.blocked, publish.topology.invalid, import.name.invalid, layerset.default.unknown, layerset.invalid, package.invalid 500 server.error 503 server.busy

OPTIONS on a Builder route gets 204 and the same Allow header as a 405 answer for that path, and does nothing else.

More about issues in answers:

  • In package.invalid, each issue has a package.* code, or, for the document of the package, a document code at a path below document.
  • A publication that goes through lists its warnings in warnings. A partial publication lists its failures in errors.
  • The Topology YAML download (POST /builder/export/topology) lists issues in warnings and publishBlockers. publishBlockers has one issue for each check that only publishing makes, with the code of its first issue.
  • POST /builder/package lists its package.* warnings in warnings.

The dependencies of POST /builder/package/resolve are data, not issues, and have no codes. The warnings of an import or a legacy diagram conversion (POST /builder/generate, POST /builder/legacy, and the source.warnings of a document) are plain text, without codes.

docs.title: Templates and Icons
docs.text: A device template holds the fields of a new device: its icon, colors, layer and the whole node spec. A custom icon is an image of your own on a device, a group or an icon drawing.

docs.title: Where templates live
docs.text: Place What it is This diagram Templates saved in the diagram, which go everywhere the diagram goes. Library One library on the phēnix server, shared by all its users. Built-in Five read-only templates: Server, Workstation, Router, Firewall and External device. Server Template files that an administrator put on the server, as read-only collections.

docs.title: Add a device from a template
docs.text:
Under Templates in Nodes & Objects, the sections are This diagram, Library or Other library templates, each collection, and Built-in. Click a template, or drag it onto the canvas.

The new device has the hostname of the template, with a number when the diagram already has that name, for example plc-2. It has a connection point for each interface of the template, and no connections. It has the icon, icon size and layer of the template. A change to the template changes no device.

When you add a device from a library template or a server template, Builder also adds a linked copy to This diagram (see Linked templates).

docs.title: Make a diagram template
docs.text:
To save ws-01 of Riverside Water as a template of the diagram:

  1. Select ws-01 on the canvas.
  2. Click New device template, the + beside Templates.
  3. Change Template Name from ws-01 to Engineering workstation.
  4. Enter Template Description CORP workstation with CAD tools.
  5. Click Save to diagram.

The template shows under This diagram. Undo reverses the save. A template made from a device keeps all of the device except its connections. With no device or with several nodes selected, the template starts from a plain device.

In the template editor, Hostname is the name that new devices start from (see The template editor).

Each template of This diagram has a menu with Edit, Save to library and Delete. A linked template also has Unlink, and Update when its source has a newer version. Save to library adds a copy to the library and links the template to it. Delete asks no question, and Undo brings the template back.

docs.title: Linked templates
docs.text:
A linked template is a diagram template that is a copy of a library template or a server template. A mark under the template says when it needs your attention, for example Update available or Deleted from library.

To update a linked template:

  1. Click Update on its mark, in its menu, or in the Inspector.
  2. Read the question. It says if the update replaces your changes to the template.
  3. Click Update template.

Devices made from the template do not change. Update all in the Inspector updates every linked template with a newer version. Unlink ends the link and keeps the template as it is (see Linked templates).

docs.title: The template library
docs.text:
To see the library, click the Node Templates tab on the drafts page. In the editor, click Node Templates library beside Templates.

The tab has New template, New collection and Import templates. Show selects the list: All library templates, Templates with missing images, a collection, Built-in templates, or a server collection. Each library card has Edit, Delete and Download. A read-only card has View, Duplicate and Download.

Save in the template editor sends the template to the server, and Undo cannot reverse this. Delete asks first. It deletes the template for all users, and diagrams keep their copies, which then show Deleted from library.

docs.title: Collections
docs.text:
A collection is a named group of library templates, and a template can be in several. To make a collection:

  1. Click New collection.
  2. Enter a Name.
  3. Click Create collection.

To fill it, select templates under All library templates. Then select the collection in Add to collection. While a collection shows, Edit collection changes its name and description. Delete collection deletes it and keeps its templates (see Collections).

docs.title: Missing disk images
docs.text: A card with a drive image that the server does not have shows a warning. Templates with missing images in Show lists only those templates. The check needs a role that can list disk images (see Missing disk images).

docs.title: Template files
docs.text:
A template file holds one collection of templates, as YAML or JSON. A download also carries a copy of each custom icon that its templates name and the server has. Download on a card, Download selected and Download collection each save a template file.

To import a template file:

  1. Click Import templates on the Node Templates tab.
  2. Select the file. Builder describes it, for example "Plant floor: 2 templates and 1 custom icon."
  3. Click Import.

Import adds the templates to a new collection, named by the name in the file. For the format, see File formats and the example node-templates.yaml.

docs.title: Server collections
docs.text: Each template file in the template directory of the server becomes one read-only collection, shown as Server: and its name. See Template files on the server. Duplicate collection copies it into the library, where you can change the copy.

docs.title: Custom icons
docs.text:
All users of the server share one icon library. To use a custom icon:

  1. Select the device, the group or the icon drawing.
  2. In the Inspector, click Icon.
  3. At the end of the list, select Custom icon….
  4. In the Custom icons dialog, click Use on a listed icon. Or click Upload icon… and select an image file.
  5. For an upload, enter the icon name. Then click Add icon.

Upload icon… takes a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG file of at most 5 MiB. The icon name is unique on the server. The change takes effect at once. A custom icon keeps its own colors in the light and the dark theme, so use an image that is clear on both.

docs.title: The Icons tab
docs.text:
The Icons tab of the drafts page lists the built-in icons and the server icons. View shows an icon at its stored size and at three small sizes. Download saves it as PNG. Delete deletes an icon that a user uploaded, after a question.

Rename in the Custom icons dialog gives a new name to an icon that a user uploaded, and the old name still works. Deleting an icon changes no diagram: its nodes show their built-in icon until someone uploads an icon of that name (see Renaming and deleting icons).

docs.title: Icons in a diagram file
docs.text: A draft names its icons. Except for a copy that it kept from an uploaded file, it holds no image of them. A Builder JSON or YAML download carries a copy of each icon that the diagram names. An upload adds the icons that the server does not have (see The diagram and its icons).

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text:
• The library, a diagram and a template file each have limits. See Limits.
  • Each template card has a checkbox, and a row above the cards acts on the selection. See Selecting several templates.
  • The Custom icons dialog lists the copies that the diagram holds under In this diagram, and Add selected to server adds several at once. See Several icons at once.
  • When Builder cannot read the library, Templates says so, with Retry. See When the library cannot be loaded.
  • Scripts manage the library through the REST API. See From a script.

docs.title: More detail
docs.text:
• Templates: details: every rule and message of templates and collections.
  • Custom icons: every rule of the icon library.
  • Built-in templates and Built-in icons.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page lists what you can see when something goes wrong in Builder, why it happens, and what to do. The exact messages, codes, save states and limits are in the Reference, and most rows link to the page that has more.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: What you see Why What to do No Builder link in the navigation bar, or "Your role does not include the Builder." The role has no builder use permission. Ask an administrator for the Builder role, or for the builder policy. See Permissions. A button is missing or unavailable, for example Publish or Import. The role does not allow that task. A published diagram also opens read only, without Publish. See What each task needs and Published diagrams. "Only Builder can edit this configuration" on the Configs page The topology has a Builder diagram, and the role has no builder use. Ask for the builder policy. See From the Configs page. "Your role cannot publish diagrams." in the command palette The role has no configs update. Ask for the permission, or let a user with the Builder role publish the draft. "The Builder does not check drive images, because the server did not list its disk images." The role has no disks list, or the server lists no images, for example while minimega is not running. Nothing. The other checks still run. See Checks and warnings. "Topology … does not exist, or you do not have permission to read it." Someone deleted the topology, or the role cannot list it. Ask for configs list and topologies list on the topology. "You cannot save changes to this draft" The role no longer includes Builder. Ask for the permission. Click Download to keep a copy.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
The save state is after Draft History in the toolbar (see Save states):

What you see Why What to do The save state says "Offline: …" The browser cannot reach the server, or the server did not answer in time. The browser keeps the changes. Keep the tab open, or click Retry saving. See Working offline. "This draft changed on the server" Someone saved a newer version of the draft first. A change clashes with yours, the merged diagram has an error, or merging is not available. Click Review and merge, Save my history as a new draft or Discard mine and load the server version. See Draft merging. "This draft is also open in another tab" You opened one draft in two tabs. Close one tab. When both tabs hold unsaved changes, choose which to save in Choose which changes to save. See Same draft in multiple tabs. "Could not save: someone deleted this draft from the server. …" Another user deleted the draft. Click Download to keep a copy, then upload the file as a new draft. "Could not save your last change. …" The server refused the diagram, for example two devices with one hostname. The message names the issue. Fix the issue. The next change saves the diagram. See Checks and warnings. The sign-in page opens while you work The session ended, by default after 24 hours. Log in. The logout deleted the changes that the server did not have. See Logging out. A notice above the toolbar counts the newer snapshots that your next change deletes You restored or undid to an older snapshot. To keep the newer snapshots, click Return to latest or Save newer history as a new draft. See Newer snapshots. A draft card says "You cannot open this draft, because the Builder cannot read it. A newer version of phenix may have saved it." A newer phēnix saved the draft. Open the draft with that phēnix version, or delete it. See Damaged drafts. The server refuses a new draft, and says to delete drafts or to run Clean up… The server holds 2,000 drafts, its limit. Delete drafts, or click Clean up… in Settings. See Limits.

docs.title: Publishing
docs.text: What you see Why What to do "N errors block publishing" under Checks The diagram has errors, or one of the five warnings that block publishing, for example an interface with no VLAN. Click Go to beside each issue and fix it. See What blocks publishing. "A topology with this name already exists. This diagram cannot update it. …" The draft did not come from that topology and did not publish to it. For a topology from the legacy Builder, only the draft imported from it can update it. Publish under another name, or import the topology and change that draft. See Publish again. "A topology with this name changed after this diagram published it. Publishing would overwrite that change. …" Someone changed the topology outside Builder after this draft published it. Import the topology again, or publish under another name. See Publish again. "This diagram comes from topology …. That topology changed on the server after Builder made the diagram. Publish refuses this diagram under any name. …" The source config changed after Builder made the draft, by import, by upload of a document made from it, or from its published diagram. Make a new draft of the config, and copy your changes into it. See When the source config changed. "Could not publish the diagram. Scenario … does not exist.", or "Not found on the server" beside a scenario in the Scenarios dialog The diagram lists a scenario that does not exist, or that the role cannot read. Store the scenario, or ask for configs get and scenarios list on it. Or clear its checkbox and click Save scenarios. See The list of scenarios. "Could not publish the diagram. Adding topology … to scenario …: user … does not have permission" The role cannot update a scenario that the diagram lists. Ask for configs update on the scenario, or clear its checkbox in the Scenarios dialog. "phenix cannot publish topology …: node … is in this topology and in its included topology …" The diagram and an included topology use one hostname. Rename the device here, or in the included topology. See Included topologies. "Published with failures. …" A stage failed after the server wrote earlier stages, for example because the experiment is running. Fix the cause, for example stop the experiment. Then click Back and publish again with the same names. See Publish results. The result warns about deleted host pins The experiment update deleted the spec.schedules pins of VMs that are no longer in the topology. To keep a renamed VM on its host, edit spec.schedules, or schedule the experiment again. See Host pins. "Could not publish the diagram. Topology … or its Builder file changed after Builder opened this draft from the file." or "Could not publish the diagram. Topology … is not what its Builder file publishes. …" The topology names a Builder file. The file or the topology changed, or the topology is not what the diagram in the file publishes. Publish under a new topology name. See Publishing to a topology that names a Builder file.

docs.title: Import and upload
docs.text: What you see Why What to do Upload refuses a Topology or Experiment config A config is not a diagram. Click Import and choose Config file. See Import a config file. Upload refuses a template file or a layer set file Each has its own place. Click Import templates on the Node Templates tab. Click Upload layer set… on the Layers tab. "This is possibly a legacy Builder diagram (XML). Select "Legacy Builder diagram or Topology" to convert it." The file is XML. In Upload, choose the source Legacy Builder diagram or Topology. See Converting a file. "Could not convert the legacy diagram. …" The file is not a legacy Builder diagram, or it is a Topology config without the builder-xml annotation. See Converting a file. The import dialog lists warnings The import changed or omitted something, for example an interface with white space in its VLAN, or an included topology that you cannot read. Read each warning, then click Continue to editor. See What an import keeps. A package upload shows Missing, Different or Not checked items The server does not have the item, has another version, or cannot check it. Tick Create on this server for a missing config in the package. Builder adds the missing custom icons itself. Add the other items yourself. See Uploading a package. "Could not open the diagram of topology …. Builder file …" phēnix cannot use the Builder file that the topology names. The message says why. See When the file cannot be used. phenix config create skips a file as a "Builder document", or refuses it as "not a configuration" The file is a Builder document, a package, a template file or a layer set file, not a config. Upload a document or a package in Builder. Click Import templates on the Node Templates tab for a template file, or Upload layer set… on the Layers tab for a layer set file. See Builder documents and phenix config create. phenix config create refuses a topology with "builder-doc.path: must be an absolute path" or a similar reason The builder-doc annotation is not valid. Fix the annotation. See What phenix checks.

docs.title: Libraries
docs.text: What you see Why What to do "The Builder could not load the template library." with Retry Builder could not read the library from the server. Click Retry. The diagram templates and the built-in templates stay listed. "The Builder cannot read the template library. A newer version of phenix may have saved it." A newer phēnix saved the library. The server refuses each library change. Use that phēnix version. The tab still lists the built-in templates and the server collections. See When the library cannot be loaded. "The server cannot read 1 layer set. A newer version of phenix may have saved it." on the Layers tab A newer phēnix saved that layer set. The list omits it. Use that phēnix version. The tab still lists the other layer sets. "Could not load the server's icons." with Retry on the Icons tab Builder could not read the icon library from the server. The tab says why. Click Retry. See The Icons tab. Update available or Deleted from library under a template, or a mark that the server collection no longer has it The library template changed, someone deleted it, or the server collection no longer has it. Click Update or Unlink. See Linked templates. Icon shows "(custom icon not found: the node shows its built-in icon)" Someone deleted the icon, or the diagram came from another server. Upload an icon of that name. See Custom icons. "The Builder could not convert this image. Save it as a PNG, and then upload it again." The browser could not make a PNG icon from the file, for example an SVG that draws nothing on its own. Save the picture as a PNG and upload that. "icon name "…" belongs to an icon … uploaded. Choose another name" The server has another image under that name. Enter another name. "The layer set has a newer version. Update from the layer set first." Someone saved the layer set after the diagram copied it. Click Update from layer set. It replaces your changes to the copy. Make your changes again, then click Save to layer set. See Layer sets. "Could not save the template. A library holds at most 200 templates." The library is full. Delete templates that nobody uses. See Limits.

docs.title: Other problems
docs.text: What you see Why What to do "Auto layout failed. The layout engine could not start." or "Auto layout failed. The Builder could not load the layout engine. Reload the page to try again." A proxy or a content security policy may block the layout engine. Reload the page. Ask the administrator to let the proxy serve the phēnix scripts and to allow workers from the same origin. See Availability. "The Builder could not check the pattern. Reload the page to try again." in Auto-group by name pattern The same cause: the policy may block the pattern check. Reload the page. "This pattern takes too long to match. Use a simpler one." The regular expression took more than 2 seconds. Use a simpler pattern. See Grouping by a name pattern. "Nothing to group: …" in Auto-group No ungrouped device or switch matches, or a group would have one member. For By name pattern…, change the pattern. Otherwise select other nodes, or ungroup first. See Auto-group. A Preflight check shows Unavailable The role lacks the permission of the check, Builder cannot connect to minimega, or the server lists no disk images. Or the check took longer than 20 seconds. Read the cause under the check. The other checks still run. See Preflight. A draft opens at the Default layout although it had one The draft named a layout of an earlier Builder version, such as Yifan Hu. Select a layout in the layout menu. See Layouts. The Icon size field says that your setting overrides it Your Node icon size setting is not Off. Other users see the sizes of the diagram. Set Node icon size to Off in Settings. See Your own icon size and hidden icons.

docs.title: Tutorial
docs.text: In about 10 minutes, you import a topology, arrange it, add a workstation, fix a warning, and publish a topology and an experiment. The example is Riverside Water, a small water utility with an internet edge, a DMZ, a corporate network and an OT network behind a firewall.

docs.title: The example lab
docs.text:
You need a phēnix server, and a role that can use Builder, such as Global Admin or Builder (see Administration).

Download these files:

  • corp-services.topology.yaml
  • riverside-water.topology.yaml
  • riverside-water.scenario.yaml

Store the three configs, and create the experiment riverside from them. From the command line:

phenix config create corp-services.topology.yaml riverside-water.topology.yaml riverside-water.scenario.yaml
phenix experiment create riverside -t riverside-water -s riverside-water

Or use the Web-UI. Upload the three configs on the Configs page (see Create a Config). Then create the experiment riverside on the Experiments page, with the topology and the scenario riverside-water (see Create a New Experiment).

The other pages use more example files: pump-station.topology.yaml, pump-station.builder.json, pump-station.package.yaml, riverside-water.builder.json, lakeside-treatment.builder.json and node-templates.yaml. You do not need them now.

docs.title: Step 1: Import the topology
docs.text:
1. Click Builder in the navigation bar. The drafts page opens.
  2. Click Import.
  3. In the Import topology or experiment dialog, select riverside-water under Source name. Keep the other fields as they are.
  4. Click Import. The dialog says "This import has 1 warning." The warning says that dns-01 and ntp-01 come from the included topology corp-services and are read only.
  5. Click Continue to editor.

A new draft named riverside-water opens in the editor, with its devices in rows on a grid. Builder saves every change that you make from now on. The toolbar shows the save state, for example All changes saved.

docs.title: Step 2: Arrange the diagram
docs.text:
1. In the toolbar, open the layout menu. It says Default.
  2. Select ELK layered. Each switch moves next to its devices.
  3. Click Auto-group. Select By network. Builder puts each network in a group: CORP, DMZ, INTERNET and OT.
  4. Click Fit diagram to view at the bottom left of the canvas.

The two devices with a dashed border, dns-01 and ntp-01, come from the included topology corp-services. You can move them, but you cannot change them here.

docs.title: Step 3: Add a workstation
docs.text:
1. Under Templates in the left column, click Workstation. A device named workstation appears on the canvas, and the Inspector on the right shows its settings.
  2. In the Inspector, set Hostname to ws-03 and Description to Engineering workstation.
  3. Under Network, click Add interface. The new interface is eth0, with Interface kind Static or OSPF and Mask 24.
  4. Enter Address 10.10.20.103, Gateway 10.10.20.1 and VLAN CORP.
  5. Click Apply.

Builder connects eth0 to the CORP switch, because the VLAN names that network. The header now counts 13 devices and 16 connections, and says No issues. On a server that lists its disk images, the header can also show a warning for an image that the server does not have. That warning does not block publishing (see The Editor).

Tip

You can also connect a device with the mouse. Drag from the + handle under the device to a switch. Builder adds the interface and, when the network has a subnet, gives it the next free address.

docs.title: Step 4: Fix a warning
docs.text:
Builder checks the diagram while you work. To see a warning:

  1. Select historian-01 on the canvas.
  2. Press Ctrl+D (⌘+D on macOS). A copy named historian-01-2 appears, with an interface that is not connected. The header says 1 warning.
  3. Click 1 warning. The Diagram checks dialog says that eth0 of historian-01-2 has no VLAN.
  4. Click Go to beside the warning. The canvas selects the copy.
  5. Click Delete in the toolbar. The header says No issues again.

A warning like this blocks publishing, because the experiment would fail or operate incorrectly with it. Other warnings only inform you. See The Editor.

docs.title: Step 5: Add the scenario
docs.text:
To give the experiment a scenario, add it to the diagram. The diagram lists the scenarios that it uses:

  1. Click Scenarios in the toolbar.
  2. Under Scenarios of this diagram, select the checkbox of riverside-water.
  3. Click Save scenarios.

docs.title: Step 6: Publish
docs.text:
1. Click Publish in the toolbar. The Publish diagram dialog opens.
  2. Under What to publish, select Topology and an experiment.
  3. Keep Topology name riverside-water. The hint says "A topology with this name exists. Publishing updates it."
  4. Enter Experiment name riverside-lab.
  5. Keep Experiment scenario riverside-water.
  6. Read Checks. It says that 11 devices, 4 switches, 4 networks and 14 connections are ready to publish. Publish does not copy the two included devices: the topology includes corp-services by reference.
  7. Click Update topology and create experiment. Builder asks "Replace topology riverside-water?".
  8. Click Update topology and create experiment again.
  9. The dialog says "Published. Every stage succeeded." Click Close.

phēnix keeps no earlier version of a config. Before Builder replaces a config, it always asks. See Publishing.

docs.title: Step 7: Open the result
docs.text:
• The Topology config riverside-water now has ws-03. On the Configs page, its row has the tag builder. Click the tag to open the diagram in Builder again.
  • The experiment riverside-lab is on the Experiments page. In the editor, Exp in the toolbar opens it. To start it, see Experiments.
  • Publish does not update experiments that you made outside Builder, such as riverside.

docs.title: Step 8: Download a picture
docs.text:
1. Click Download in the toolbar.
  2. Click PNG. The browser saves riverside-water.png.
  3. Click Close.

The same dialog saves the diagram as Builder JSON, which Upload opens, or as Topology YAML, the Topology config that Publish would write. To move the diagram to another phēnix server, download a Builder package. See Import, Upload and Download.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Builder saves each later edit to the same draft. To publish the changes, click Publish again with the same names. See Publishing.
  • To go back to an earlier version, click Draft History in the toolbar. See Drafts.
  • To draw more, see Diagrams. To reuse device settings, see Templates and Icons.
  • When something does not work as this page says, see Troubleshooting.
