docs.title: Administration: details
docs.text:
Info

This page holds every rule, limit and message of this feature. For the short guide, see Administration.

This page is for phenix administrators.

docs.title: Availability
docs.text:
Each phenix server has the Builder, and no setting turns it on or off. Roles control who can use it (see Permissions). The editor is at /builder, and its API is under /api/v1/builder (see REST API).

phenix sets no Content-Security-Policy on the application page. If a proxy in front of phenix adds one, the policy must allow workers from the phenix origin and data: images. The layout engine and Auto-group by name pattern run in workers. Custom icons are data: images.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
The permission builder use gives a user the Builder. With it, a user reads and changes all the Builder data of the server: every draft, the three libraries, and the Builder schemas that give the fields of the Inspector.

Drafts have no owner. Any Builder user can open, change and delete any draft. A draft records who created it and who changed it last, for information only.

To give a role the Builder, add this policy to it:

- resources:
  - builder
  verbs:
  - use

The policy takes no resource names. The verb "*" also gives use.

builder use gives no access to phenix configs (see What each task needs and Resource: configs). A role that limits topology names does not limit which Builder files its users can read (see Who can read a Builder file).

With authentication disabled, all users work as global-admin, with the Global Admin role (see User Authn/Authz in phenix). Drafts then show global-admin as the user who created and changed them.

Of the built-in roles, only Global Admin and Builder have builder use. Global Viewer does not. Give Builder users the Builder role, or a role such as the example role.

docs.title: The Builder role
docs.text:
The built-in role Builder (builder) is for users who draw and publish topologies. It holds:

  • builder use.
  • configs list, get, create, update and delete, on Topology/*, Scenario/* and Experiment/* only. It gives no access to User, Role or Image configs.
  • schemas get, topologies and scenarios list and get, experiments list, get, create and update, and disks list.

Builder (builder) shows the role as YAML.

Each time phenix ui starts, it makes sure that the role exists:

  • When the store has no role named builder and no role with the role name Builder, phenix creates the role. Thus a deleted role comes back.
  • When the role exists, phenix keeps its policies. If the role has no builder use, phenix adds the builder policy to the role and to its users. Nothing else changes.

phenix does not change other roles. Add the builder policy to each other role that must use the Builder. Assign a role on the Users page (see Updating Users).

docs.title: What each task needs
docs.text:
builder use alone allows these tasks: all work on drafts and snapshots, undo and redo, the libraries, the default layer set, the Inspector fields, and Upload of a Builder document from a file or pasted text. The other tasks also need the permissions in this table.

Task Other permissions See the Published Diagrams tab configs list on the topologies that it lists Open a published diagram, with Open, Edit as a draft or Upload configs get on that topology, such as Topology/riverside-water. This does not protect a Builder file (see Who can read a Builder file) Import a stored config configs get on the config, and topologies list (or experiments list) on its name Import a config file, or convert a legacy Builder diagram with Upload configs get and create Upload a Builder package configs get. To create the configs that you tick, also create Open a topology in Builder from the Configs page configs list, and get on the topology. To import it, also create See Exp, which opens the experiment of a publication experiments get on that experiment Add a stored scenario to a diagram configs list and scenarios list Store a scenario file from the Scenarios dialog configs create on Scenario/<name>. To replace a scenario, configs get and update on it See the apps of the diagram's scenario in the Inspector configs get on Scenario/<name> Download Topology YAML or a package configs get Use Publish, in the editor or on a draft card configs update Publish a topology configs create on Topology/<name> for a new topology, update for an existing one. For a draft imported from a stored config, also configs get and topologies get (or experiments get) on that config Publish an experiment experiments create and configs create on Experiment/<name>. To update one, update of both Publish a diagram that lists scenarios configs get and scenarios list on each listed Scenario/<name>. It also needs configs update on each scenario whose topology annotation does not name the topology yet Delete a published topology configs delete on Topology/<name> Get drive image suggestions and missing-image checks disks list Run Preflight checks configs get, and for each check: Host capacity, hosts list. Networks, hosts list for the bridges, experiments list for the VLANs of running experiments (only those it can list by name), and configs get and experiments get on the named experiment. Disk images, disks list. Scenario apps, applications list, and configs get and scenarios list on each listed Scenario/<name>. Without its permission, a check or a part of it shows as unavailable

Import and Publish read included topologies, such as corp-services, with the configs get and topologies list permissions of the user. They warn about an include that the user cannot read.

An import of a config file keeps each ${NAME} and ${NAME:default} as written. Thus the Builder never shows the environment variables of the server (see Importing a config file).

docs.title: The libraries
docs.text:
The server keeps one template library, one layer set library and one icon library. All Builder users share them (see The template library, Layer sets and Custom icons). builder use allows each change.

No role can change these items, Global Admin included:

  • The five built-in templates, and the templates and collections of the template files on the server. A change answers 409 with the code template.item.read-only.
  • The built-in layer set Purdue Model (ID builtin:purdue). A change or a delete answers 403 with the code layerset.read-only.
  • The icons that phenix adds from template files. A rename or a delete answers 403.

Duplicate makes a copy of a read-only template or layer set that users can change. Any Builder user can rename or delete an uploaded icon.

The server has one default layer set (see Layers for new diagrams). When a user deletes it, the server has no default. A diagram keeps its own copies of templates and layers, so a library change does not change the diagram (see Linked templates).

phenix logs each library change with the user name: each add, change or delete of a template, collection or layer set, each choice of a default layer set, and each upload, rename or delete of an icon.

docs.title: Example role
docs.text:
The example role Topology Designer cannot publish, import a config file or delete a topology. It also cannot store a scenario file or create the configs of a package. It can do all other work on drafts and the libraries, import stored configs, open published diagrams and download Topology YAML. A user with the Builder role can then publish its drafts. Download it from topology-designer.role.yaml:

apiVersion: phenix.sandia.gov/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: topology-designer
spec:
  roleName: Topology Designer
  policies:
  - resources:
    - builder
    verbs:
    - use
  - resources:
    - configs
    resourceNames:
    - "Topology/*"
    - "Scenario/*"
    - "Experiment/*"
    verbs:
    - list
    - get
  - resources:
    - topologies
    - scenarios
    - experiments
    resourceNames:
    - "*"
    verbs:
    - list
    - get
  - resources:
    - disks
    resourceNames:
    - "*"
    verbs:
    - list

Do not use "*/*" in the configs policy. It also matches User and Role configs, so a user could read password hashes. To let the role publish, add create, update and delete to its configs policy.

To add the role, store it as a config, then assign it on the Users page:

phenix config create topology-designer.role.yaml

Note

phenix copies the policies of a role into a user when you assign the role. After you change a Role config, assign the role to its users again.

docs.title: What users without a permission see
docs.text:
Builder hides, or makes unavailable, each control for a task in What each task needs that the role does not allow. The server still checks each request.

  • Without builder use, there is no Builder link, and the Configs page has no Builder links or buttons. /builder shows only "Your role does not include the Builder." Each Builder API request answers 403.
  • Without configs update, the command palette gives the reason "Your role cannot publish diagrams."
  • Without disks list, the Diagram checks dialog says "The Builder does not check drive images, because the server did not list its disk images." It says the same when the server lists no images, for example while minimega is not running.

A refused request answers 403, with a message such as "deleting a Builder draft: user bob does not have permission". A draft that does not exist answers 404.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Drafts, published documents and the three libraries are records in the phenix store (the store.endpoint setting), not configs. phenix config list and the Configs page do not list them.

Limits:

  • The server holds at most 2,000 drafts, damaged drafts included. Past it, POST /builder/drafts answers 413 with the code draft.limit, and a message that says to delete drafts or to run Clean up. GET /builder/drafts reports the limit as limits.drafts.
  • A draft keeps at most 50 snapshots and 50 MiB of them. Past either limit, phenix deletes the oldest snapshots.
  • A diagram (a Builder document) can be at most 5 MiB. It can hold at most 50 custom icons, 50 device templates and 100 notes of its own.
  • The server holds at most 2,000 icons. The built-in icons are not part of this limit, but the Icons tab counts them. An icon is a PNG of at most 96 × 96 pixels and 40,960 bytes.
  • The template library can be at most 512 KiB, with at most 200 templates and 50 collections (see Limits).
  • The layer set library holds at most 200 layer sets, and the built-in Purdue Model. A layer set has 1 to 32 layers, and a layer has at most 16 node matchers. A request that adds or replaces a layer set can be at most 1 MiB, and a layer set file at most 4 MiB. A full library answers 413 with the code layerset.library.full.

The libraries belong to the server. When someone deletes a user account, its icons, templates and layer sets stay, and createdBy and updatedBy keep the user name. The built-in templates and layer set are part of phenix, not store records. A template library that never changed has no record. phenix keeps the collections of its template files in memory only.

Drafts and published documents use these store namespaces:

  • builder.drafts: one record for each draft, with its ID as the key. It holds the metadata of the draft and its snapshots, not the documents.
  • builder.content: one gzip record for each document. The key is drafts/ and the draft and snapshot IDs, or published/ and the document ID. phenix checks the size and the sha256 digest at each read.
  • builder.published: one record for each published document, with its ID as the key.

Each save, undo or redo, snapshot delete and draft delete writes all its records in one store transaction. Thus the store never holds a draft without its documents, or a part of a failed save. Each stored value has a small header with its revision and times.

The libraries use these store namespaces:

  • builder.icons: one record for each icon name, with the key name/ and the name in lower case. An icon with old names has a record for each.
  • builder.templates: one record, library, with all the templates and collections.
  • builder.layersets: one record for each layer set, with the key set/ and its ID, and the record default when a user chose a default set.

A publish stores a copy of the diagram that never changes, the published document. The builder-doc annotation of the topology names it (see The builder-doc annotation). After a publish, phenix deletes the older published documents of the topology that are more than one hour old.

When anyone deletes or renames a topology, by any means, phenix deletes its published documents. A document less than one hour old can stay for a time, because a publish may be in progress. Deleting or renaming a topology never reads, changes or deletes a Builder file (see Renaming and copying a topology).

The browser also keeps some Builder data:

  • The IndexedDB database phenix-builder keeps changes until the server stores them.
  • localStorage keeps preferences: phenix.builder.theme, phenix.builder.panes, phenix.builder.minimap, phenix.builder.shortcuts and phenix.builder.settings. The last one holds the Settings dialog choices, such as Snap to grid, and whether Show connections is on. They apply to that browser, not to the diagram.
  • The Builder does not read phenix.builder.layers, the default layers of earlier versions. Logging out deletes the key.
  • Logging out, or signing in as another user in the same browser, deletes the rest: unsaved changes, recent commands, the last Auto-group name pattern, the last Preflight checks (phenix.builder.preflight) and the collapsed sections of Templates (phenix.builder.palette). See Logging out.

docs.title: Cleaning up storage
docs.text:
When phenix starts, and each hour while it runs, it deletes the published documents that no topology references. It also deletes the documents in builder.content that no draft and no published document names. It keeps:

  • what phenix stored in the last hour, because a publish or a save may still reference it
  • every published document, when a topology cannot be read or its builder-doc annotation does not decode
  • a published document that it cannot read, and its content
  • every Builder file

phenix leaves a published document that it cannot read out of every list, and logs "skipping unreadable builder published document" with the ID. A newer phenix may have saved it. To delete it, send DELETE /builder/documents/{document} with that ID. This deletes only the record and its content, and changes no config. When the record still names its topology, the role needs configs get and delete on it. Otherwise the role needs them on */*, as Global Admin has. If-Match must name the tag of the stored record. Send any tag, and the 412 answer gives the tag in its ETag header.

Clean up… in the Builder settings does the same at once. It also deletes each draft that has no change since its last publish. For such a draft, the current snapshot is the last one it published, no newer snapshot follows it, and its topology still references what it published. The topology and its published document stay. These drafts also stay:

  • A draft whose topology someone deleted, or published again from another draft. It is then the only copy of its diagram.
  • A draft that changes while the cleanup runs.

A cleanup waits for a publish that is in progress.

With ?dryRun=true, POST /builder/cleanup deletes nothing and tells what it would delete:

{"dryRun": true, "drafts": ["4b0c…"], "documents": 1, "content": 2}

drafts lists draft IDs. documents and content count published documents and documents in builder.content. When the cleanup cannot read or delete an item, the answer has a Warning header, and the server log gives the reason. The answer still lists the deleted drafts.

docs.title: Template files on the server
docs.text:
To give all users the same node templates, put template files in the template directory of the server. When phenix ui starts, it reads each file as one read-only collection (see Server collections). A file has the format that the Node Templates tab downloads (see Downloading and importing templates and the example node-templates.yaml).

The directory is <base-dir.phenix>/builder/templates, by default /phenix/builder/templates. To change it, set base-dir.builder-templates with the root flag --base-dir.builder-templates, the environment variable PHENIX_BASE_DIR_BUILDER_TEMPLATES, or the phenix config file (see Settings):

base-dir:
  builder-templates: /etc/phenix/builder-templates

phenix reads at most 50 files directly in the directory, in name order. It reads only names that end in .yaml, .yml or .json, in any case, and not names that start with .. It does not read subdirectories. A file must be a regular file of at most 8 MiB, as JSON or YAML. phenix follows a symbolic link only when the link stays in the directory. phenix skips a file that is not valid, and reads the others.

phenix logs:

  • skipping builder template file, a warning with the directory, the file and the reason. An example reason is is not a valid template file: templates[1].name: template name "plc" is also the name of templates[0], ignoring case.
  • A directory that does not exist, at debug level only.
  • builder template directory cannot be read, a warning, when the path is not a directory.
  • read builder template files, with the number of collections read and of files skipped.

When the directory does not exist or cannot be read, phenix has no server collections, and the Builder starts.

phenix adds the custom icons of a file to the icon library, under their names, when the library does not have them. These icons have no uploader. The icon dialog shows them as from "Server", and no user can rename or delete them. They fill at most 1,000 of the 2,000 icons. phenix skips icons past that limit, and logs one warning, builder icon library has no room for more template file icons, with the number skipped. When the library has an icon of the same name with a different picture, the library keeps its picture. phenix then logs builder template file icon differs from the icon library's, which is kept with the file, the icon and the owner of the library icon (the server for an icon from a template file).

phenix reads the directory only when it starts. Restart phenix ui after you add, change or delete a file. phenix writes only the new icons to the store, not the collections.

phenix makes the ID of each collection and template from the file name and the template name. The IDs stay the same across restarts. A renamed file gives its collection a new ID. A diagram links its copy of a template by that ID (see Linked templates).

docs.title: The builder-doc annotation
docs.text:
A topology names its diagram in the builder-doc annotation of its Topology config. The annotation is a map with up to three keys:

apiVersion: phenix.sandia.gov/v1
kind: Topology
metadata:
  name: pump-station
  annotations:
    builder-doc:
      digest: sha256:1c92d3b0c95588fbb20926c1e58bb0452903c4e2cb0ffbf12fcdc19f72717732
      id: fd063e784604f43e5c39cc9959501cf117b4dc2be895e92f9bb98e23f8465c4b
      path: /phenix/topologies/pump-station/pump-station.builder.json
Key What it holds digest sha256: and 64 lowercase hex digits. It names the stored published document with that content for this topology. With path, it sets which document the file must hold. id The ID of a published document in the store. It applies only to the topology that received the document. path The absolute path of a Builder file on the phenix server (see Builder documents in files).

The map must have at least one of these keys, and no other keys. Publish writes digest and id, and keeps a path. You write path yourself.

builder-doc is the only annotation that is a map, or in JSON, an object. All other annotations are text.

docs.title: Which diagram a topology shows
docs.text:
1. The published document that the annotation names: by id, or by digest when there is no id. It must belong to this topology, and must match the digest, if any.
  2. Otherwise, the Builder file at path. It must hold the document with the digest, if any.
  3. Otherwise, none. Published Diagrams does not list the topology. On the Configs page, its builder tag and its edit button open the Import dialog, with "Topology pump-station has no Builder diagram to open. Import it to make one."

The stored document comes first because Publish wrote the stored topology from it. The file may have changed since then.

docs.title: What phenix checks
docs.text:
phenix checks the annotation each time anyone creates or updates a Topology config, by any means. It refuses a config whose builder-doc is not valid. With phenix config create, the log line before the error gives the reason:

$ phenix config create pump-station.topology.yaml
2026-10-01 21:52:35.595 ERR calling config hook: config validation failed: topology pump-station: builder: invalid request: builder-doc.path: must be an absolute path type=SYSTEM uuid=197b8a05-ccb3-4162-994a-c39d8ebc1dc5
Error: Unable to create configuration from pump-station.topology.yaml (search error logs for 197b8a05-ccb3-4162-994a-c39d8ebc1dc5)
Reason What is wrong value must be an object builder-doc is text, not a map property "file" is unsupported A key other than digest, id and path there must be at least 1 properties The map is empty builder-doc: digest is not a sha256 digest digest is not sha256: and 64 lowercase hex digits builder-doc.path: must be an absolute path path does not start with / builder-doc.path: must be a clean path, with no ".", "..", "//" or trailing "/" path has one of these builder-doc.path: must end in .json, .yaml or .yml path has a different ending, or an ending in capitals, such as .JSON

A path can be at most 1024 bytes. phenix does not look for the file when it stores the config.

phenix config edit cannot delete an annotation. To delete builder-doc, send the config without it with PUT /api/v1/configs/topology/<name>. Or delete the topology and create it again.

docs.title: Renaming and copying a topology
docs.text:
A published document belongs to one topology name. After a rename, or a copy of the config under a new name, the id and digest no longer name a document of that topology. phenix then changes the annotation:

  • Without a path, phenix deletes the annotation. The topology is a plain Topology config until someone publishes it again.
  • With a path, phenix deletes the id. The path and the digest stay, so phenix reads the topology from the file. The file must still hold the document with that digest.

docs.title: Builder documents in files
docs.text: A topology can name a Builder document in a file on the phenix server, instead of a published document. Use this for topologies in a repository that you check out on the server. The diagram then opens in Builder without a publish.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
The directory /phenix/topologies/pump-station/ holds two files:

  • pump-station.builder.json, the Builder document (the example file pump-station.builder.json).

  • pump-station.topology.yaml, the Topology config, with a builder-doc annotation that names the document:

    apiVersion: phenix.sandia.gov/v1
kind: Topology
metadata:
    name: pump-station
    annotations:
        builder-doc:
            path: /phenix/topologies/pump-station/pump-station.builder.json
spec:
    nodes:
        - general:
            description: Field engineering laptop
            hostname: eng-ws-01
        # ... the rest of the nodes

To make the Topology config:

  1. Open the document in Builder.
  2. Click Download > Topology YAML (see Topology YAML).
  3. Set metadata.name.
  4. Add the annotation. Do not change the spec.

If the topology differs from what the document publishes, a draft made from the file cannot update it (see Publishing to a topology that names a Builder file). For this reason, do not use the example file pump-station.topology.yaml here. Its node order is different.

Store the config:

$ phenix config create /phenix/topologies/pump-station/pump-station.topology.yaml
2026-10-01 21:52:35.788 INF configuration created type=SYSTEM kind=Topology name=pump-station

Published Diagrams then lists pump-station with the tag File. Its diagram opens read only (see Diagrams read from a file).

phenix reads the file each time and keeps no copy. Thus after a git pull changes the file, the next Open shows the new diagram. The stored Topology config does not change. To make it match the file again, create the config again, or publish a draft made from the file.

docs.title: Which files phenix reads
docs.text:
phenix reads a Builder file only when all of these conditions are true:

  • The file is below the phenix base directory: /phenix, or the base-dir.phenix setting (see Settings).
  • It is not below the VM mount directory: /phenix/mounts, or the mount-dir setting.
  • It is a regular file, not a directory, a device or a pipe. phenix follows a symbolic link only when its target is a relative path that stays below the base directory and outside the mount directory. phenix refuses an absolute target, such as from ln -s /phenix/topologies/a.json b.json.
  • It is at most 5 MiB.
  • It holds one valid Builder document, as JSON or YAML. The content sets the format, not the file name. A YAML file must not use anchors, aliases, merge keys or more than one document.

When the CLI creates the config from a file, phenix fills in ${NAME} in the path from the environment. A config sent to the REST API fills in only ${BRANCH_NAME}. phenix does not fill in ${NAME} in the Builder file.

phenix resolves the path on the server that runs phenix ui. When several phenix servers share one store, each server reads its own file system.

phenix reads the file only when someone opens the diagram, makes a draft from it, or publishes that draft to the topology. Published Diagrams reads no file, so it shows a card even when the file is missing or not valid. No config change and no phenix command reads the file.

docs.title: Who can read a Builder file
docs.text:
Anyone whose role has configs get on the topology can open its diagram. Anyone who can list the config can see the path.

Warning

The name of a topology does not protect its Builder file. A user who has configs get, and create or update, on any one topology name can store a topology there with any path below the base directory. The user can then open the diagram of that file.

For example, a role limited to Topology/teama-* cannot read the topologies of team B. But its users can store teama-x with the path of a Builder file of team B, and open it. A fixed layout such as /phenix/topologies/<name>/ makes the path easy to guess.

Keep a Builder file below the base directory only when each user who can create or update a topology may read it. A published document does not have this problem, because it belongs to its topology.

docs.title: Pinning the file with a digest
docs.text:
Add digest beside path to accept one document only:

    builder-doc:
      digest: sha256:1c92d3b0c95588fbb20926c1e58bb0452903c4e2cb0ffbf12fcdc19f72717732
      path: /phenix/topologies/pump-station/pump-station.builder.json

When the file holds a different document, the diagram does not open.

The digest is the SHA-256 of the document as phenix writes it, not of the file. sha256sum of a YAML file, or of a JSON file with different spacing, key order or final line break, gives a different value. To get the digest, use the REST API (see Examples).

docs.title: When the file cannot be used
docs.text:
Opening the diagram then fails with "Could not open the diagram of topology pump-station." and one of these sentences. Each sentence names the path, but not the file content. The REST API gives the same sentence as message. The phenix log gives builder document file not usable, with the topology, the path and the reason.

Message Status Why "Builder file … is outside /phenix, the directory phenix reads Builder files from." 422 The path is not below the base directory, or it is below the mount directory "Builder file … does not exist on this phenix server." 404 No file is at the path, or a part of the path is a file "phenix cannot read Builder file …." 422 phenix has no read permission, a symbolic link is not allowed, or the read failed "Builder file … is not a regular file." 422 The path is a directory, a device or a pipe "Builder file … is larger than 5 MiB." 413 The file is too large "Builder file … is not a valid Builder document. Upload it in the Builder to see why." 422 The file is not a valid Builder document. Upload shows the problem (see Uploading a Builder document) "Builder file … does not match the digest topology pump-station records for it." 422 The file holds a document with a different digest

docs.title: Editing and publishing
docs.text:
Edit as a draft makes a draft from the file (see Diagrams read from a file). For when that draft can update the topology, see Publishing to a topology that names a Builder file.

Publish never writes the file. It stores a published document and writes digest and id beside the path:

    builder-doc:
      digest: sha256:4ba9ae46494bb7d2498f5119b55996f332c52c1b95d79502361afbf50707cbc3
      id: 89f0a9779c2e5892da9f7a9ae2ed5c58c564fe57ea86f50f4452f174cb68ad93
      path: /phenix/topologies/pump-station/pump-station.builder.json

The topology then shows the published document, without the File tag. The file is out of date until you replace it. The path stays for a different phenix server that gets this config without the published document. That server reads its own file, if the file matches the digest.

docs.title: REST API
docs.text:
Scripts use the same REST API as the web UI, under /api/v1. The interactive API docs of a running server, at /docs/, describe each route under the Builder tag (see Interactive API Docs).

No single request publishes a Builder file. Create a draft from the document, then publish the draft.

Each route needs builder use. These routes also need configs permissions:

Route What it does configs permission POST /builder/drafts/{draft}/publish Create or update the Topology and Experiment configs, and add the topology to the topology annotation of each listed scenario. With "dryRun": true, tell what publishing would change, and write nothing. A dry run needs no If-Match The permissions of each config POST /builder/drafts/{draft}/preflight Run the preflight checks named in checks (capacity, network, disks, apps) on the current document, against the named experiment, if any get, and the permissions of each check (see What each task needs) GET /builder/sources The configs that a document can come from or publish with list POST /builder/generate Make a document from a stored Topology or Experiment config, or a config file, with the import options (includes, copy, name) get. create for a config file POST /builder/legacy Convert a legacy Builder diagram, or a Topology config file that holds one, into a document get and create POST /builder/export/topology The Topology YAML that a document would publish get POST /builder/package The Builder package of a document, with the sections in include get. For each config in the package, get with scenarios or topologies list POST /builder/package/resolve For each item that the package diagram needs: present, missing, different or unknown on this server get. list for icons, disks list for disk images, applications list for apps GET /builder/documents List the published documents (source store), and the topologies that name a Builder file (source file, with path and no id) list GET /builder/documents/{document} Read a published document get on its topology DELETE /builder/documents/{document} Delete a published topology and its published documents, or an unreadable published document (see Cleaning up storage) get and delete on the topology GET /builder/topologies/{topology}/document Read the diagram that builder-doc names, from the store or the Builder file get on the topology

These routes need only builder use:

Route Notes GET /schemas/builder/v1, /schemas/builder/templates/v1, /schemas/builder/package/v1, /schemas/builder/layersets/v1 The JSON Schemas of the Builder document, a template file, a Builder package and a layer set file GET, POST /builder/drafts The list has drafts, latest change first, damaged (drafts that this server cannot read) and limits.drafts GET, DELETE /builder/drafts/{draft} GET gives the current document. DELETE also deletes a damaged draft GET, POST /builder/drafts/{draft}/snapshots POST saves a new version of the document GET, DELETE /builder/drafts/{draft}/snapshots/{snapshot} current names the current snapshot, which DELETE cannot delete PATCH /builder/drafts/{draft}/cursor Undo and redo: choose the current snapshot POST /builder/cleanup See Cleaning up storage GET, POST /builder/icons The list has no images. It gives maxIcons and an etag. With If-None-Match of that tag, it answers 304 while the list does not change. POST uploads a PNG under a name GET, PUT, DELETE /builder/icons/{icon} GET reads an icon and its image, by its name or an old name. PUT renames an uploaded icon, and keeps at most 16 old names. DELETE deletes an uploaded icon and all its names GET /builder/templates The library (templates, collections), the built-in templates (builtins) and the server collections (preloaded) POST /builder/templates/items, PUT /builder/templates/items/{template} Add templates, and with collection, a new collection that holds them. Replace a template POST /builder/templates/collections, PUT /builder/templates/collections/{collection} Add or replace a collection POST /builder/templates/delete Delete templates and collections GET, POST /builder/layersets The list has the built-in sets first, then the others by name. It gives defaultId, defaultEtag, damaged (records that this server cannot read) and the limits GET, PUT /builder/layersets/default Read or choose the default layer set. "id": null clears the choice GET, PUT, DELETE /builder/layersets/{layerset} PUT and DELETE do not accept a built-in set

A change to a read-only library item answers as The libraries tells.

These requests need an If-Match header with the etag of the item from the last response: each change to an existing draft, PUT and DELETE of a layer set, PUT of a template or a collection, PUT /builder/layersets/default, and DELETE of an icon or a published topology. A request without it answers 400. An older tag answers 412 (template.item.stale, layerset.stale or request.stale) with the current ETag. Then read the item again, check it, and send the request again. POST /builder/templates/delete names each item with its etag in the body ({"templates": [{"id": "…", "etag": "\"3\""}]}). When one of them changed, it answers 412 and deletes nothing.

Draft responses also have the ETag in their body, as etag. Use that value, because a proxy that compresses responses can change the ETag header. The etag of an icon changes at a rename. The etag of a published topology changes at each change of the topology.

Each template, collection, layer set and icon in a response has createdBy (who added the item) and updatedBy (who changed it last). An item that no user added, such as a built-in template, has no createdBy.

With authentication enabled, send a token in the X-Phenix-Auth-Token header, as Bearer <token> (see Generating User Authentication Tokens).

A refused request answers with a JSON body whose code names the failure, such as publish.topology.exists. When a document is not valid, or only publishing refuses a draft, issues lists each problem with its own code. The warnings and failures of a publication are issues too. Error Codes lists every code.

docs.title: Response headers
docs.text:
Each Builder response, the schema routes included, has X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, because each response is JSON. Each also has Cache-Control: no-store, so no browser or proxy keeps a copy, also of an error or a 304 answer.

The icon responses hold the images as base64 in the JSON. They also have Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'. If a browser shows one of them as a page, it loads, runs and frames nothing.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
These examples use the example lab (see Builder Examples) and jq. Set the server and your token first:

PHENIX=http://localhost:3000
TOKEN='your-token'   # a token from the Users page

List the drafts:

curl -s -H "X-Phenix-Auth-Token: Bearer $TOKEN" "$PHENIX/api/v1/builder/drafts" \
  | jq '.drafts[] | {title, createdBy, id, etag}'

{
  "title": "Riverside Water",
  "createdBy": "darrow",
  "id": "6290aef3-24a3-4126-b90a-308cbf561f17",
  "etag": "\"10\""
}

Make a document from the stored topology riverside-water, as Import does. POST /builder/generate writes nothing:

curl -s -X POST -H "X-Phenix-Auth-Token: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"source":"Topology/riverside-water"}' "$PHENIX/api/v1/builder/generate" > generated.json
jq '{name: .document.metadata.name, source: .source.fullName, warnings}' generated.json

{
  "name": "riverside-water",
  "source": "Topology/riverside-water",
  "warnings": [
    "The Builder added 2 nodes from included topology corp-services (2 nodes). The diagram shows them read only. Edit them in their own topology. Publishing keeps includeTopologies and does not copy them."
  ]
}

Store the document as a draft. The sourceToken connects the draft to its topology, so the draft can publish back to riverside-water:

jq '{title: .document.metadata.name, sourceToken: .source.fullName, document}' generated.json \
  | curl -s -X POST -H "X-Phenix-Auth-Token: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d @- "$PHENIX/api/v1/builder/drafts" > created.json
jq '{id, createdBy, title, etag}' created.json

{
  "id": "6b471c7d-dd32-44e7-ae85-a889f377747f",
  "createdBy": "darrow",
  "title": "riverside-water",
  "etag": "\"14\""
}

To keep the name of an uploaded file, which the Inspector shows as Source file, send sourceFile beside document. It must be a plain file name of at most 255 bytes, with no / or \.

The server writes who made and last saved the diagram into its metadata (see Who made and last saved a diagram). The answers to creating and saving a draft have no document. They give createdBy, createdAt, updatedBy and updatedAt as stamp.

Convert a legacy Builder diagram, as Upload does. content is the XML of the diagram, or a Topology config that holds it in builder-xml. name names a diagram that has no topology. The answer has the same form as for POST /builder/generate:

jq -Rs '{content: ., name: "plant"}' plant.xml \
  | curl -s -X POST -H "X-Phenix-Auth-Token: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      -d @- "$PHENIX/api/v1/builder/legacy" > converted.json
jq '{name: .document.metadata.name, warnings}' converted.json

Delete the draft with its current ETag. The delete answers 204, or 400 without If-Match:

ID=$(jq -r .id created.json)
ETAG=$(curl -s -H "X-Phenix-Auth-Token: Bearer $TOKEN" "$PHENIX/api/v1/builder/drafts/$ID" | jq -r .etag)
curl -s -X DELETE -H "X-Phenix-Auth-Token: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "If-Match: $ETAG" \
  "$PHENIX/api/v1/builder/drafts/$ID"

Read the diagram of the topology pump-station (see Builder documents in files), without the document:

curl -s -H "X-Phenix-Auth-Token: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  "$PHENIX/api/v1/builder/topologies/pump-station/document" | jq 'del(.document)'

{
  "source": "file",
  "digest": "sha256:1c92d3b0c95588fbb20926c1e58bb0452903c4e2cb0ffbf12fcdc19f72717732",
  "size": 6517,
  "target": "pump-station",
  "kind": "Topology",
  "config": "Topology/pump-station",
  "path": "/phenix/topologies/pump-station/pump-station.builder.json"
}

digest is the digest to write beside path (see Pinning the file with a digest). For a file, the answer has "topologyDiffers": true when the stored topology is not what the document publishes. For a published document, source is store, and the answer has id, createdBy and createdAt, not path.

docs.title: Compressed files
docs.text:
The Builder page loads large script files that other pages do not load. The UI build writes a Brotli copy and a gzip copy of each, when the copy is smaller. phenix sends the copy that the browser accepts, and tells the browser to keep the file for one year. A changed file gets a new name, so browsers get it after an upgrade.

The environment variable PHENIX_BROTLI_QUALITY sets the Brotli quality of the UI build: a whole number from 0 to 11, by default 9. A higher quality makes smaller copies and a slower build. Another value stops the build with an error.

The Docker and Podman images both build from docker/Dockerfile, which sets quality 11. make docker uses docker/Dockerfile. make deb builds docker/Dockerfile, then makes the package from that image. When PHENIX_BUILD_IMAGE names an image that you built before, make deb uses that image and its quality. All other builds, such as make build and npm run build, use quality 9.

To build the UI with quality 11:

cd src/js
PHENIX_BROTLI_QUALITY=11 npm run build

To build the Docker image with a different quality:

docker build --build-arg PHENIX_BROTLI_QUALITY=9 -t phenix -f docker/Dockerfile .

docs.title: Checks and Preflight: details
docs.text:
Info

This page holds every rule, limit and message of this feature. For the short guide, see The Editor.

docs.title: Checks and warnings
docs.text:
Builder checks the diagram while you edit it. The checks button in the header shows the result: No issues, or a count such as 3 warnings.

To fix an issue:

  1. Click the checks button. The Diagram checks dialog lists the errors, then the warnings.
  2. Click Go to beside the issue. The canvas selects its node, and the Inspector shows it.
  3. Fix the field. In the Inspector, Go to beside an issue moves focus to its field.

Some issues also have Fix (see Fixing an issue in one step).

Go to shows a hidden Inspector and moves the view to the node. An issue about a network goes to its switch. An issue that names no field moves focus to its node or connection. An issue about the full diagram, or about a network with no switch, has no Go to.

There are two levels:

  • Errors, such as an empty required field. You cannot publish until you fix them.
  • Warnings. Some warnings block Publish, which lists them as errors (see What blocks publishing). The dialog says so. Other warnings, such as a device with no interfaces, do not block publishing.

For the full list of codes, see Codes.

The canvas marks each node and connection with an issue: a cross for an error, or a triangle for only warnings. Screen readers read the issues as the description of the item.

Devices from included topologies get no warnings, because they belong to their own topology. But a hostname that an included device also uses is an error, and an address that it also uses is a warning.

When the server lists no disk images, the dialog says "The Builder does not check drive images, because the server did not list its disk images." Otherwise, a drive image that the server does not have is a warning.

docs.title: Rulesets and addresses
docs.text:
phenix accepts these settings, but they do not work as the diagram shows them. None of these warnings blocks publishing. Publish and the Topology YAML download also list them.

Warning Code Go to opens A device that is not a Router or a Firewall has firewall rulesets, or an interface that names one. The vrouter app ignores them. device.rulesets.ignored The Type of the device An Inbound ruleset or Outbound ruleset of an interface names no ruleset of its device. The vrouter app then applies no firewall to that interface. interface.ruleset.unknown The ruleset field The address of an interface is not a host address of the subnet of its network. interface.ip.outside-subnet The Address No interface on a network has the gateway address of the network. Interfaces of external devices and of included topologies count. network.gateway.unowned The Gateway of the network The subnets of two networks overlap. network.subnet.overlap The Subnet of the network

Overlapping subnets are a problem only when the networks connect, for example through a router. Isolated enclaves that reuse a subnet on purpose can ignore this warning.

docs.title: Device settings
docs.text:
phenix apps do not apply these device settings as the diagram shows them. The Inspector shows the same warnings at the field. Publish and the Topology YAML download also list them. Three of them block publishing (see What blocks publishing).

These devices get fewer warnings:

  • Devices from included topologies and external devices get none of these warnings. phenix still reads the ntp-server label of an external device.
  • phenix apps do not configure a device whose phenix/default-apps annotation is false. It gets no warning about its OS type, interfaces, OSPF or vrouter/enable-ssh.
  • That device still gets the warnings about no drive, file injections, phenix/startup-autotunnel and the ntp-server label.
Warning Code Go to opens A device has no drive under Drives. phenix needs a drive to start it. This blocks publishing. device.drives.none Add drive under Drives A Router or Firewall has an OS type other than vyatta, vyos or minirouter. phenix does not configure its routing or firewall. phenix still configures linux as Vyatta, but this is deprecated. device.router-os.unsupported OS type A device that is not a Router or Firewall has static interfaces. Its OS type is not linux, rhel, centos or windows, for example other. phenix writes no interface configuration for it. device.interfaces.unconfigured OS type A device has serial interfaces, but its OS type is not exactly linux. phenix sets serial interfaces only on linux. device.serial.unconfigured OS type A device has file injections or deletions, but Snapshot is off, or the Inject partition of its first drive is 0. phenix does not inject or delete its files. device.injections.unapplied Snapshot, or the Inject partition of the drive A Vyatta or VyOS router (OS type vyatta, vyos or linux) has an interface with protocol ospf, but no network.ospf. The experiment does not start. This blocks publishing. device.ospf.missing The Protocol of the interface An ospf interface of a minirouter has an address in no area network of its network.ospf, or the device has no network.ospf. The interface is in no OSPF area. interface.ospf.outside-area The Address of the interface An area network of a minirouter holds the address of none of its ospf interfaces. minirouter does not advertise it. device.ospf-network.unused The area network A minirouter has network.ospf, but no interface with protocol ospf. device.ospf.unused network.ospf The ntp-server label names no interface of its device, or an interface with no IP address. The experiment does not start. This blocks publishing. device.ntp-server.invalid The value of the label More than one device has the ntp-server label. phenix uses only the first device with it, in the order of the diagram. device.ntp-server.ignored The value of the label The diagram has Vyatta or VyOS routers, and the ntp-server device has no interface on VLAN mgmt, in any case. The routers get no NTP server, unless an ntp app of the scenario names one. device.ntp-server.no-mgmt The value of the label The vrouter/enable-ssh annotation of a Vyatta or VyOS router is not an IP address or the name of an interface with an IP address. phenix does not enable SSH. phenix reads this annotation on no other device. device.enable-ssh.invalid The value of the annotation An entry of the phenix/startup-autotunnel annotation is not "port", "port:dport" or "port:host:dport", with ports from 1 to 65535. A dport of VNC, in any case, permits an empty host. phenix skips each bad entry. phenix opens no tunnel when the value is not a list of texts. device.autotunnel.invalid The value of the annotation The phenix/default-apps annotation is not true or false, for example the text "false". phenix runs its default apps. device.default-apps.invalid The value of the annotation

phenix finds an interface by name in any case: ETH0 names eth0. In the Inspector, the values of the ntp-server label and the vrouter/enable-ssh annotation suggest the interface names of the device.

docs.title: Fixing an issue in one step
docs.text:
Some issues have a Fix button, which says what it does, for example "Fix: Rename web-01 to web-01-2". The dialog stays open, and focus moves to the next issue. Undo reverts each fix as one step.

Issue Code What Fix does Two devices have the same hostname node.hostname.duplicate Renames the device to the next free hostname, such as web-01-2. When the other device is from an included topology, Fix renames the device of this diagram. Interfaces on one network use the same IP address interface.ip.shared Gives the interface the first free address of the subnet, as Assign addresses does, with the same gateway rules. Interfaces on one network use the same MAC address interface.mac.shared Clears the MAC address of the interface. phenix then makes one when the experiment starts.

There is no Fix in these cases:

  • The draft is read only.
  • The device is from an included topology, which must fix it.
  • For an IP address: the interface is on no network, its network has no subnet, or the subnet has no free address. Set a Subnet for the network, or type a new address in the Inspector.
  • For a router interface with the gateway address: the router keeps the gateway. When several routers have the gateway, the first router keeps it. Fix gives each other router a free address.

docs.title: Preflight
docs.text:
The Preflight section of Diagram checks asks the phenix server to check the saved draft against the server and its cluster. The checks write nothing and start no VM or experiment. This browser keeps the checks that you ticked last until you log out.

Check What it compares Host capacity The hardware.vcpus and hardware.memory of each device that is not external, against the free resources of the schedulable cluster hosts. Unset values count as 1 vCPU and 512 MB. Each device must fit on one host. A device that fits on no host fails the check. Too little free memory fails it. Too few free CPUs is a warning, because VMs can share CPUs. Networks The VLANs of the devices and the VLAN aliases of the networks, against the VLAN range of the experiment that you name. No range applies without an experiment, or when the experiment sets none. The aliases, against the VLANs of the running experiments that your role may list. The summary says when it left out experiments that your role may not list, but it does not name them. The bridges of the interfaces and the default bridge of the experiment (phenix without an experiment), against the bridges of the schedulable hosts. A missing bridge is a warning, because minimega creates it when the experiment starts. Disk images Each drive image, by file name, against the disk images of the server. The kind must agree: a VM or ISO image for a kvm device, a container image for a container. The server keeps its list of disk images for 10 seconds, so it may not find a new image yet. Scenario apps Each app that the scenarios of the diagram run, against the default apps, the built-in apps and the user apps on the PATH of the server. Disabled apps do not count.

To run Preflight:

  1. Click the checks button in the header.
  2. Under Preflight, tick the checks.
  3. Optional: in Experiment (optional), type the name of the experiment.
  4. Click Run. Builder first saves your latest changes.

The report gives a total, for example "Preflight: 3 passed, 1 unavailable". Each check shows Passed, Failed or Unavailable, and a summary. Each issue has its code. An issue about a device or a network has Go to.

A check is Unavailable when Builder could not do all of it. An issue gives one of these causes:

  • Your role does not have the permission that the check needs (see Administration).
  • Builder cannot connect to minimega.
  • The server lists no disk images, or does not list them within 10 seconds.
  • The check took longer than 20 seconds.

Builder still does the other checks. The report stays until the diagram changes.

docs.title: Building a Diagram: details
docs.text:
Info

This page holds every rule, limit and message of this feature. For the short guide, see Diagrams.

This page shows how to draw and change a diagram. For the parts of the editor, see The Editor. Icons, Layers and Scenarios and Included Topologies have their own pages. The examples use the Riverside Water draft of the example lab.

docs.title: Devices, switches and connections
docs.text:
A diagram describes one phenix Topology config:

In the diagram In the published Topology A device A node in spec.nodes, with its settings A switch A network. Its name is the VLAN of each interface on it A connection from a device to a switch An interface of the device, with the network's name as its vlan A device from an included topology Nothing: includeTopologies names that topology Notes, groups, shapes, icons, lines, colors, line styles, icon sizes, custom icons, layers and the diagram's templates Nothing

docs.title: Adding devices
docs.text:
To add a device from Nodes & Objects, at the top of the left column, do one of these steps:

  • Click the item. The device appears in free space in the visible part of the canvas, or outside it when that part is full. Builder selects it.
  • Drag the item to the canvas.
  • In the command palette (⌘+K/Ctrl+K), choose Add device, then select a template.

Device adds a device with default settings. The templates under Templates set more settings. The table lists the Device item and the five built-in templates, which the Built-in section always lists:

Item Hostname Type OS type Image Device node VirtualMachine linux ubuntu.qc2 Server server VirtualMachine linux ubuntu.qc2 Workstation workstation VirtualMachine windows windows10.qc2 Router router Router minirouter minirouter.qc2 Firewall firewall Firewall vyos vyos.qc2 External device external HIL (external) None None

The built-in templates are read only. To change one, duplicate it into the template library of the server (see Node Templates).

To add an engineering workstation to Riverside Water:

  1. Under Templates, click Workstation.
  2. In the Inspector, set Hostname to ws-03 and Description to CAD workstation.
  3. Click Apply.

docs.title: Routers and firewalls
docs.text: The vrouter app configures the interfaces, routes and rulesets of a device of type Router or Firewall (see vrouter App). For a VyOS router, such as edge-rtr, set OS type to vyos and the drive's Image to vyos.qc2.

docs.title: External devices
docs.text: An external device is hardware that the experiment connects to, such as a PLC. phenix starts no VM for it, so it has no image. Its interfaces tell phenix which VLANs the hardware is on (see External Nodes).

docs.title: Adding switches and networks
docs.text:
A switch is one network. To add a network:

  1. Under Nodes & Objects, click Switch, or choose Add switch in the command palette. A switch appears, with a new network named EXP, then EXP-2 and so on.
  2. In the Inspector, set Name, for example SCADA, and click Apply.

When you rename a network, the VLAN of each interface on it changes.

A switch's outline has the color of its network's connections, unless the switch has its own Outline Color (see Colors). A screen reader names the switch, its network and its VLAN alias.

The Inspector of a switch has these network fields:

  • VLAN alias: optional, from 1 to 4094. When you publish with an experiment, it becomes the network's entry in vlans.aliases (see Publishing a topology and an experiment).
  • Subnet: an optional IPv4 network in CIDR form, such as 10.1.0.0/24.
  • Gateway: an optional IPv4 address of the router on the network. It must be a host address of the subnet, such as 10.1.0.1 in 10.1.0.0/24.

To find a network, type # in the command palette. Remove network in the command palette deletes a network, its switches and their connections. A network can have more than one switch, for example after a paste.

When you delete the last switch of a network, Builder deletes the network in the same edit. Undo restores both. The network stays when the VLAN of an interface with no connection still names it. The checks then warn that the network has no switch. To correct this, add a switch, change the VLAN, or use Remove network. A diagram that you open or upload keeps all its networks.

docs.title: Subnets and addresses
docs.text:
Builder uses a network's Subnet and Gateway to give addresses to the static interfaces on the network. A static interface has the Interface kind Static or OSPF. Builder gives an address only to a static interface that has no address. It never changes an address that an interface has, or a device from an included topology.

An assigned address is the next free host address of the subnet. A free address is not the gateway, and no other interface on the network uses it. The interface also gets the subnet's prefix length as its Mask. When the interface has no Gateway, it gets the network's gateway. For example, with the subnet 10.1.0.0/24 and the gateway 10.1.0.1, the first interface gets 10.1.0.2, mask 24 and gateway 10.1.0.1.

A router holds the gateway. Here, a router is a device of type Router or Firewall. Router interfaces get their addresses first, and never get a Gateway of their own:

  • When no interface on the network has the gateway address, the first router interface gets it.
  • When the network has no gateway, the first router interface gets the next free address. That address becomes the network's Gateway in the same step, and the interfaces after it get that gateway.
  • Other router interfaces get the next free addresses.

A new network gets a suggested subnet. It is the first 10.N.M.0/24 that overlaps no subnet of the diagram. It also holds no interface or gateway address of the diagram. In an empty diagram, that is 10.1.0.0/24. You can change or clear it. A network that you import or upload keeps its own subnet, or has none.

Builder gives addresses at these times:

  • When you connect a static interface to a switch of the network: with a drag, with Add a connection, or with Paste or Duplicate of a device and its switch. After a drag or Add a connection, Builder says the address, for example "Set the address of eth0 of ws-03 to 10.1.0.2/24."
  • When you click Assign addresses in the Inspector of a switch, or choose it and the network in the command palette. This is one step of Undo, for example "Assigned 3 addresses on network SCADA".

The Assign addresses on connect setting, in the Editing section of Settings, is on by default. When it is off, a connection, paste or duplicate gives no address. After a drag or Add a connection, Builder then says "No address set. Type an address for eth0 of ws-03 in the Inspector, or select Assign addresses." Assign addresses and the suggested subnet work with the setting on or off.

A network without a subnet gives no address. When you connect a static interface to it, Builder says "No address set: network CORP has no subnet. Type an address for eth0 of ws-03 in the Inspector." Assign addresses is then not available. When the subnet is full, Builder says, for example, "No address set: subnet 10.1.0.0/30 of network SCADA is full."

A static interface without an address stops Apply of its device.

docs.title: Connecting interfaces
docs.text: A connection puts a device's interface on a network. Each example below connects ws-03 to CORP. CORP has no subnet, so eth0 gets no address. Type its address in the Inspector, for example 10.10.20.103, or give CORP a subnet first.

docs.title: Drag on the canvas
docs.text:
1. Point at ws-03. Each interface has a connection point (a circle) on the device's sides. A + handle is at its bottom.
  2. Drag from the + handle, or from an unconnected connection point, to the CORP switch.

A drag from + adds a new static interface. A published diagram and a device from an included topology have no + handle.

A drag from one device to another adds a switch between them, with a new network named EXP and a suggested subnet. You cannot connect two switches, because each switch is one network.

docs.title: Add a connection without dragging
docs.text:
1. Select a device or a switch.
  2. Click Add connection (the link button) in the Inspector header, or choose Add a connection… in the command palette. The dialog opens with the selection filled in.
  3. In Device, choose ws-03.
  4. Keep Interface set to Add a new interface, or choose an interface that has no connection.
  5. In Switch, choose CORP (CORP).
  6. Click Connect.

The command has no default key (see Customizing shortcuts).

The dialog stays open in these cases:

  • A field is empty. Connect names it and moves focus to it.
  • Builder cannot make the connection. The dialog says why.

docs.title: Type the VLAN in the Inspector
docs.text:
When you apply a network's name in an interface's VLAN field, Builder connects the interface to that network's switch. The quick start connects ws-03 this way:

  1. Select ws-03.
  2. In the Inspector, under Network, click Add interface. The new interface eth0 is Static or OSPF, with Mask 24.
  3. Enter Address 10.10.20.103 and Gateway 10.10.20.1.
  4. Enter VLAN CORP.
  5. Click Apply. Draft History names the change "Updated device ws-03 and connected eth0 to network CORP".

The VLAN matches a network's name in any letter case. The name of another network moves the connection. A VLAN that names no network stays, but the interface stays unconnected. A typed VLAN gives no address.

A renamed interface keeps its connection while its VLAN names the same network. When you remove one interface and add another in the same Apply, the new interface does not get the old connection. It connects only when its VLAN names a network.

docs.title: Disconnecting
docs.text:
To disconnect an interface, do one of these steps:

  • In the Inspector's Connection points, click Disconnect next to the interface, for example "eth0 — network CORP".
  • Select the connection on the canvas and press ⌫ on macOS or Delete on Windows and Linux.

The interface stays, with no VLAN, and blocks publishing (see What blocks publishing). Connect it again, type a VLAN, or remove it with Remove connection point (the trash button). Add connection point adds a static interface with no connection and no address. The buttons under Connection points take effect at once, without Apply.

docs.title: Hiding connections
docs.text:
To hide the connections on your canvas, choose Hide connections in the command palette, or press ⌥+⇧+C (Alt+Shift+C) outside a text field. The same command, now Show connections, shows them again. The Show connections switch in Settings does the same.

This changes only your canvas. This browser keeps your choice for the next diagram. The diagram, its checks, Publish and the downloads keep every connection: a PNG or SVG still draws them. While connections are hidden:

  • You cannot click, select or focus a connection. Select all selects only nodes.
  • Go to on an issue about a connection selects the node it starts at.
  • The marks of connections with errors or warnings do not show.
  • A drag from a connection point still connects it.
  • PgDn and PgUp do not move through connections.

docs.title: Editing device settings
docs.text:
Change the fields of a device in the Inspector or the Node Editor, then click Apply (see Editing a node).

An interface has an Interface kind:

  • Static or OSPF: an address that you give, or that Builder gives from the subnet. A new interface is this kind, with Mask 24. When you add an interface in the Inspector, focus goes to its Address.
  • DHCP or manual: the address comes from DHCP, or from a setting inside the VM.
  • Serial: a serial link.

An interface of an external device has no Interface kind. It is a static interface with Mask 24.

When you change the kind, Builder asks, for example, "Switch Interface kind to DHCP or manual?" Switch and clear changes the kind and empties all fields of that interface, Name and VLAN included. Keep current value changes nothing. Set the kind first.

A device shows its Description on the canvas. The eye button beside the field hides it (see Hiding descriptions on the canvas).

Generate a random MAC address, beside MAC address, writes a locally administered unicast address that no other interface of the diagram uses. Click Apply to keep it.

docs.title: Duplicating a device
docs.text:
Duplicate pastes a copy of the selected nodes next to them (see Copy, paste, duplicate and delete). The copy keeps every setting, addresses included, but not its connections.

To add a second historian:

  1. Select historian-01.
  2. Press ⌘+D (Ctrl+D). The copy historian-01-2 appears, with the address 10.10.30.20 and an unconnected eth0.

The header then says 1 warning: eth0 of historian-01-2 has no VLAN. When the copy's eth0 is on the network of historian-01, the shared address is also a warning. To correct the warning, give the copy its own hostname and address, and connect it (see Example: Riverside Water expansion).

docs.title: Drive images
docs.text: When your role can list the disk images of the server, a drive's Image suggests them, and an image that the server does not have is a warning. When the server lists no images, the checks do not examine images.

docs.title: Routes and rulesets
docs.text:
Routes and Firewall rulesets are under Network. For example:

  • edge-rtr has Route 1: 10.10.30.0/24: Destination 10.10.30.0/24, Next hop 10.10.20.254 (ot-fw) and Cost 1.
  • ot-fw has Firewall ruleset 1: corp-to-ot, with Default drop and Rule 1: HTTPS to the historian. The rule accepts tcp from 10.10.20.0/24 to 10.10.30.20 port 443. The Inbound ruleset of eth0 is corp-to-ot.

The vrouter app applies them when the experiment starts. Inbound ruleset and Outbound ruleset suggest the names of the device's rulesets, unapplied ones included. The app applies rulesets only on a Router or a Firewall, and skips a ruleset name that the device does not have. The checks warn about both cases (see Rulesets and addresses).

miniccc commands, under More settings, lists the commands that phenix gives miniccc to run in the VM, such as exec df -h.

docs.title: Labels and annotations
docs.text:
A device's labels and annotations are under More settings. Each row has a Name and a Value. For example, web-01 has the labels zone: dmz and role: web, and the annotation phenix/startup-autotunnel with the value ["8080:80"]:

Builder reads an annotation value as YAML: true, false and numbers become those values, and ["8080:80"] is a list. Apps read annotations to configure a node (see Apps).

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
A note is text on the canvas. Publishing ignores it.

  1. Under Nodes & Objects, click Note.
  2. In the Inspector, enter the Text, for example OT has no route to the internet.
  3. Click Apply.

A screen reader names a note by the start of its text. A note also has a Color.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
A group is a box with a title around nodes. Publishing ignores it. When you move a group, its nodes move with it.

To group nodes:

  1. Click the first node, then Shift-click the others.
  2. Click Group in the toolbar, or press ⌘+G on macOS or Ctrl+G on Windows and Linux.

The new group is "Group", or "Group 2" and so on when that name is in use. Its Inspector has Title, Description, Color, Border pattern, Icon and Icon size:

  • The Description shows on one line under the title. Screen readers read it after the group's name.
  • Border pattern is Dashed (the default), Solid, Dotted or Double.
  • Icon is beside the title. It is the container icon by default.
  • Title and Description wait for Apply. The other fields take effect at once.

To remove a group and keep its nodes in place, select the group, then click Ungroup (⇧+⌘+G or Ctrl+Shift+G).

Group under Nodes & Objects adds an empty group. A node that you drag onto a group does not go into it. To move a node into a group:

  1. Select the node.
  2. Click Move to group (the group button) in the Inspector header, or choose Move to a group… in the command palette.
  3. In Group, choose a group, or No group to remove the node from its group.
  4. Click Move.

To resize a selected group or note, drag the handles on its corners and sides, or press ⌥+⇧ (Alt+Shift) with an arrow key. One press, or one hold, is one undo step. A group is never smaller than its members need.

docs.title: Shapes, icons and lines
docs.text:
Rectangles, circles, icons and lines are drawings. Publishing ignores them, and they take no connections. Add one under Nodes & Objects or in the command palette. The layouts do not move a drawing. A drawing in a group moves with its group. When a layout makes the group smaller, the group grows to hold the drawing.

The Inspector of a drawing has these fields:

  • A rectangle or a circle fills its box, so a circle in a box that is not square is an ellipse. It has a Label at its center, a Fill Color (without one, it is see-through), an Outline Color, a Border pattern (Solid by default), a Width and a Height.
  • An icon shows a built-in or custom icon, scaled to its box. It has an optional Label under it, a Width and a Height.
  • A line joins no node or network. It has a Label at its middle, a Color and a Line style (solid by default). It has Arrowhead at the start and Arrowhead at the end. Its Points, 2 to 64 from start to end, each have an X and a Y. A new line is 160 pixels long.

Some fields take effect at once (see Fields that take effect at once). The others wait for Apply.

Rectangles, circles and lines stay under the devices and switches, also when selected. Thus, a drawing never hides a device or its connection points.

To resize a selected rectangle, circle or icon, drag its handles, or press ⌥+⇧ (Alt+Shift) with an arrow key. A selected line shows a circle handle on each end and a square handle on each bend. Drag a handle to move its point. Double-click the line to add a bend. While Snap to grid is on, a dragged point and a new bend go to the grid. After you click a handle:

  • The arrow keys move its point by one grid step, or one pixel with ⇧.
  • Delete or Backspace removes the point. A line keeps at least two points.
  • Esc goes back to the line.

Without a mouse, use Points in the Inspector: change X and Y, or use Add point (a new end), Remove point N and Insert point after point N (a bend halfway to the next point). Apply makes all the changes as one step of Undo.

docs.title: Auto-group
docs.text:
Auto-group in the toolbar puts nodes into new groups:

  • By network: each network's switch with its devices. A device on several networks goes with the smallest one.
  • By name: devices whose hostnames share a stem, such as web-01 and web-02. Switches stay out.
  • By name pattern…: nodes whose names match a regular expression.

Auto-group groups only the devices and switches that are in no group. When nodes are selected, it groups only those. A group needs at least two members. Then Auto-group arranges the diagram with the draft's layout, so the groups do not overlap. Undo removes the groups.

For example, By network on the imported riverside-water makes the groups CORP, DMZ, INTERNET and OT.

Each choice is also a command palette command, such as Auto-group by network, which has a key (see Keyboard shortcuts).

docs.title: Grouping by a name pattern
docs.text:
1. In Auto-group, select By name pattern….
  2. In Name pattern, type a JavaScript regular expression.
  3. Click Group.

Builder matches the pattern against each device hostname and switch name, and ignores letter case. Names with the same matched text go in one group, named after that text. When the pattern has parentheses, Builder uses the text of the first pair. For example:

  • ^[a-z]+ puts web-01 and web-02 in group web, and db-01 and db-02 in group db.
  • ^(\w+)-(east|west) groups by the part of the name before the site.
  • -(\d)\d$ groups by the tens digit of the number at the end.

The rules of Auto-group apply. Limits:

  • A pattern has at most 200 characters.
  • Builder matches only the first 255 characters of a name.
  • A group's name is cut to 80 characters.
  • Builder stops a pattern that takes more than 2 seconds, with "This pattern takes too long to match. Use a simpler one."

When nothing can be grouped, the dialog says why, for example "Nothing to group: the pattern matches no ungrouped device or switch." The dialog offers your last pattern. The browser keeps it until you log out. Builder does not save it in the diagram or send it to the server.

When the pattern cannot run, the dialog says "The Builder could not check the pattern. Reload the page to try again." (see Troubleshooting).

docs.title: Colors
docs.text:
Where Field What it colors Values Switch Edge Color The network: its connections, and the outline of its switches Any CSS color Connection Color This connection, in place of its network's color Any CSS color Device, switch Outline Color The node's border #rrggbb only Device, switch Fill Color The node's background #rrggbb only Note, group Color The note or the group Any CSS color Rectangle, circle Outline Color, Fill Color The shape's border and inside #rrggbb only Line Color The line and its arrowheads #rrggbb only

To set a color, type it in the field, or click the swatch button before the field. The swatch offers Blue, Orange, Green, Purple, Red, Teal, Olive, Plum, Custom color and No color. Esc closes only the color choices, not a dialog such as the Node Editor.

A #rrggbb field takes no color names, no short form and no transparency. Another value shows "Outline Color must be a hex color, such as #2f6fbf" (or "Fill Color …"), and Builder does not apply it. The Outline Color and Fill Color of a switch belong to that switch, so two switches of one network can be different. Each color field takes effect at once.

On a fill, the text is black or white, for a contrast of at least 4.5 to 1. An outline near the canvas color gets a thin ring, so the node stays visible in both themes. In a Windows contrast theme (forced colors), Builder shows the system colors.

The outline of a device or a switch has the first of these colors:

  1. The node's own Outline Color.
  2. The color of its layer, when the diagram colors node outlines with the layer color (see Layer outlines).
  3. For a switch, the color of its network's connections.

The built-in icon of a device or a switch has the color of the node's outline, or the theme's accent color without one. A group icon always has the accent color. When the outline has a contrast of less than 3 to 1 against the node in a theme, the icon has the node's text color in that theme. On a Fill Color, the icon has the node's text color, unless the outline is a hex color with a contrast of at least 3 to 1 against the fill.

A new network gets the suggested color that the fewest networks use. The suggested colors keep their contrast in both themes.

docs.title: Line styles
docs.text:
Line style sets the line pattern on a network, for all its connections, or on one connection, in place of its network's pattern:

  • Auto: Builder selects the pattern from the network's place in the diagram, so that networks are different without color. The choice names that pattern, for example "Auto (Solid)". On a connection, Auto follows its network.
  • Solid, Dashed, Dotted or Dash-dot.

A pattern can repeat on several networks. The connection's label, its switch and its name for screen readers still name its network. Line style takes effect at once.

docs.title: Layouts
docs.text:
The layout menu in the toolbar arranges the whole diagram. It shows the layout that last arranged the draft, or Default when no layout ran. An imported, uploaded or blank draft starts at Default. An import puts its devices in rows on a grid, with the switches below them.

Layout What it does Network cards A card for each network, on a grid. In a card, the switch is at the head of a column of its devices, grouped by name. ELK layered Clusters each network's switch with its devices, a device on several networks in its smallest one. Connections run left to right between the clusters. By layer Puts the layers from top to bottom (see By layer). Dagre Each network's devices in a column beside their switch, and the networks in layers along the connections between them. Standard Every device in a row above the switches, from top to bottom.

ELK layered suits most diagrams. A layout always gives the same result for the same diagram and the same selection. ELK layered and By layer load when you first use one of them. When they cannot load, the page shows "Auto layout failed. The Builder could not load the layout engine. Reload the page to try again."

Earlier versions of Builder also had the Yifan Hu, Force and Radial layouts. A draft that names one of them opens at Default. When your Default layout setting names one of them, Builder uses ELK layered.

Layouts keep groups together. A group's members stay inside it, and no other node goes in.

For example, Metro Campus (metro-campus.topology.yaml) has 42 devices on 7 networks. These images show it after the import, then after ELK layered:

Right after a layout runs, the menu also offers Restore previous layout, until you make a different change.

Auto layout in the command palette, and its key (see Keyboard shortcuts), runs the draft's layout again. On a draft at Default, Auto layout and Auto-group use the Default layout of Settings, which is ELK layered by default.

Publishing and a Topology YAML download ignore positions and layouts.

docs.title: By layer
docs.text:
By layer arranges the diagram from top to bottom by layer, the highest layer ID at the top. Only the IDs count, so an ID that is not in the diagram's list also works. Each connection goes down from the higher layer to the lower one.

  • A device or a switch without a layer goes to the layer of the nearest connected node that has one. When two such nodes are equally near, it goes to the higher layer.
  • A connected node that no layer reaches goes below every layer. A node without connections, such as a note, goes at the bottom.
  • A group is at the layer of its highest member. Inside the group, its members are in the order of their layers.

In a diagram whose devices and switches have no layer, and inside one layer, the layout starts from a top node. Each other node goes below the node that leads to it from the top node. The top node is the first of these that the diagram has:

  1. The selected device or switch.
  2. A firewall.
  3. A router.
  4. The switch with the most connections.

The layout uses the icon or the node type to find a firewall or a router. An external device is a top node only when you select it, because hardware in the loop, such as a PLC, is usually low in a plant.

docs.title: Arranging by hand
docs.text:
• Drag a node, or several selected nodes. While Snap to grid is on, they go to the grid. A press is a click, which does not move the nodes, while the pointer stays within 4 screen pixels of the start point. With a finger or a pen, the limit is 8 pixels. When Builder cannot take a move, for example while a save conflict is open, the nodes go back.
  • Press ⇧ (Shift) with an arrow key to move the selected nodes 10 pixels. They do not snap to the grid. Hold the keys to move the nodes more. When you release a key, the move is one undo step. Screen readers announce the new position one time.
