  • Under Position in the Inspector, enter X and Y, then click Move.

A move by hand does not change the layout that the layout menu shows.

docs.title: The grid
docs.text:
Grid size, in the Inspector with nothing selected, sets the distance between the grid lines: a whole number of pixels from 4 to 200. A new diagram has a grid size of 16. Another value shows "Grid size must be a whole number from 4 to 200.", and the diagram keeps its size.

The Snap to grid setting, in the Editing section of Settings, is off by default. While it is on, these go to the nearest point of the grid:

  • Nodes that you drag, and nodes that you drop from Nodes & Objects.
  • New nodes that you add.
  • The points of a line that you drag or add.

While it is off, they go where you put them, on a whole pixel. This browser keeps the setting, and other users have their own. Snap to grid in the command palette turns it on or off.

docs.title: Copy, paste, duplicate and delete
docs.text:
Copy, Paste and Delete are in the toolbar, and Duplicate is in the command palette. Each has a key (see Keyboard shortcuts).

Copy and Paste use the Builder clipboard, not the system clipboard. They work between drafts that you open one after the other in the same browser tab. Duplicate copies and pastes the selected nodes in one step, and does not change the Builder clipboard.

  • A paste goes 40 pixels down and to the right of the original, and each next paste 40 pixels more. Builder selects the pasted nodes.
  • A pasted device gets a free hostname, such as server-2, and keeps its settings.
  • Builder pastes or duplicates a connection only with both of its nodes. Copy a device with its switch to keep the connection. With only connections selected, Duplicate does nothing and says "Select the nodes to duplicate. A copy holds a connection only with both of its nodes."
  • Copying a group copies the nodes in it.

Delete deletes the selected nodes and connections. When you delete a device, Builder also deletes its connections.

docs.title: Undo and redo
docs.text:
Undo and Redo in the toolbar, and their keys, go back and forward through your changes. Each change is a snapshot of the draft on the server, so Undo moves the draft itself back. Undo and Redo reach only the changes since you opened the draft in this tab, or since your last restore. To go back further, use Draft History.

After an undo, a new change removes the snapshots that you undid, also those that other users saved after them (see Newer snapshots).

docs.title: Drafts: details
docs.text:
Info

This page holds every rule, limit and message of this feature. For the short guide, see Drafts.

Each diagram in Builder is a draft on the phenix server. A draft is separate from the standard phenix configs. Builder saves each change to the draft as a snapshot. Builder makes a phenix Topology config only when you Publish (see Publishing).

docs.title: The drafts page
docs.text: This is the default page when you open Builder.

docs.title: Top right buttons
docs.text:
Blank diagram, Import and Upload start a new draft (see Creating a draft).

Commands opens the command palette (⌘+K on macOS, Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux).

The theme, Settings, Help and Focus mode buttons work the same as in the editor.

  • Theme: Dark, Light, or System (the light or dark appearance of your device).
  • Settings: opens Builder settings.
  • Help: opens this documentation in a new tab.
  • Focus mode: full-screen mode for focused editing (see Focus mode).

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text:
Each tab shows a count of its items, for example Drafts (3):

  • Drafts: the drafts of all users, most recently changed first. Damaged drafts come last.
  • Published Diagrams: the topologies that have a Builder diagram (see Published diagrams).
  • Node Templates: the template library. Its count includes only the library templates. The built-in templates and the server collections are under Show.
  • Layers: the layer set library, with the built-in set Purdue Model.
  • Icons: the icon library and the built-in icons. Its count includes both built-in and custom icons.

Each Builder user can open, change and delete each draft (see Permissions).

A draft card shows the name of the draft, its creator, and its last change and that user, for example "Updated Sep 29, 2026, 1:02 PM by alice". The card has a checkbox (see Selecting several drafts), Open, Duplicate, Delete, and Publish.

"Updated" is the last activity on the draft: an edit, an undo, a restore, a deleted snapshot or a publish. It can differ from Last edited in the Inspector on the Editor page, which shows when Builder saved the content (see With nothing selected).

docs.title: Item buttons
docs.text:
The buttons that act on one item, such as a draft or a layer set, look the same in all of Builder:

Button Icon Color Edit Pencil Blue Delete Trash can Red Publish Arrow up Default Duplicate Two sheets Default Open Open folder Blue View Eye Default Download Arrow down Default

An item that you cannot change has View in place of Edit.

docs.title: Filtering the lists
docs.text:
The Drafts, Published Diagrams, Node Templates and Layers tabs each have a filter field above their cards, for example Filter drafts. A line under the field shows the count, for example "2 of 12 drafts shown.".

The filters can search by:

  • Filter drafts and Filter published diagrams: the name or user (this searches users who created or last changed a draft).
  • Filter layer sets: the name or description.
  • Filter templates: the name and what t: in the command palette finds (see The Node Templates tab).

Filters match the same way as the command palette does. Each word that you type must be in the name or a user name, in any letter case. Or, the letters must be in the name in order: pmpst finds "Pump station". The words can match in different places, such as the draft name and a user name.

Filter actions:

  • Select all, Download selected and Delete selected act only on the cards that show. If a filter hides a card that you selected, Builder clears its selection.
  • Each tab keeps its filter while the browser tab is open.
  • To show all cards again, press Esc in the field, or clear it.

docs.title: Blank diagram
docs.text: Click Blank diagram. A new draft named "Untitled topology" opens in the editor. When a draft of any user has that name, the new draft is "Untitled topology 2", and so on. To rename it, see Renaming the diagram.

docs.title: Import
docs.text: Import makes a draft from a Topology or Experiment config, in phenix or in a file. The draft name matches the name of the config. See Importing a topology or experiment.

docs.title: Upload
docs.text: Upload always makes a new draft. The source is a Builder JSON or YAML file, pasted text, a published diagram, or a legacy Builder diagram. See Import, Upload and Download and Legacy Builder.

docs.title: From a published diagram
docs.text: On the Published Diagrams tab, open a card and click Edit as a draft (see Published diagrams). Edit on a Builder topology on the Configs page does the same (see Editing a published topology).

docs.title: Opening a draft
docs.text:
Click Open on the draft's card.

To open a draft from the command palette:

  1. Click Commands (⌘+K on macOS, Ctrl+K on Windows and Linux).
  2. Type open draft and press Enter. The palette lists the drafts and the published diagrams.
  3. Type part of the name and press Enter.

To go back to the list, click Drafts in the editor header. Builder saves your changes automatically.

docs.title: Links to a draft
docs.text: A link to a draft has the form <phenix address>/builder?draft=<draft id>. The address bar shows it while a draft is open, so a reload opens the same draft. The link works for each Builder user.

docs.title: Publishing from the drafts page
docs.text:
Publish on a draft's card opens the Publish diagram dialog without the editor (see Publishing).

Open draft in the dialog opens the draft in the editor. When the diagram has errors, the dialog lists them. Builder will not publish a draft with errors. The dialog then tells you to open the draft and fix any issues.

When you close the dialog, the waiting changes continue to save. Closing the dialog during a publish does not stop the publish.

docs.title: Autosave and the save state
docs.text:
Builder saves each change to the server as you make it. Each saved change is a snapshot in Draft History. There is no Save button. Save now (⌘+S on macOS, Ctrl+S on Windows and Linux) sends the changes immediately. It also applies the valid Inspector changes that you did not apply with Apply.

The save state, after Draft History in the toolbar, shows where your changes are. See save state messages.

docs.title: Working offline
docs.text:
When the server cannot be reached, Builder keeps your changes in this browser, and you can continue to edit. The save state then shows Retry saving:

Within a few seconds after the server answers again, Builder sends the changes. Retry saving sends them at once. The changes stay in this browser when you close the tab. Builder sends them the next time that you open the draft in this browser. Logging out deletes them (see Logging out).

Builder waits at most 60 seconds for the server to answer a save, and 30 seconds for a read. A save with no answer in time counts as offline, and the next try sends it again. For publishing, preflight checks, imports, exports, packages and storage cleanup, Builder waits up to 10 minutes.

docs.title: Draft History
docs.text:
Each change saved to a draft is a snapshot. Draft History in the toolbar lists the snapshots, newest first, and restores an earlier one.

For example, in the Riverside Water draft:

  1. Under Templates, click Server.
  2. In the Inspector, set Hostname to files-02.
  3. Click Apply.
  4. Click Draft History in the toolbar.

The columns are:

  • #: the snapshot number. 1 is the oldest, the draft as Builder made it.
  • Name: what the change did, for example "Added device".
  • Date and User: when and by whom Builder saved the snapshot. For the current snapshot, the Inspector shows these as Last edited. The exception is snapshot 1 of a draft made with Edit as a draft. Its row shows when you made the draft. The Inspector shows who last edited the diagram before that.
  • The Restore and Delete buttons.

Current marks the current snapshot. You cannot restore or delete it. The tooltip of each other Restore button shows how many newer snapshots your next change after the restore removes. Screen readers announce the number of snapshots and the tooltip.

docs.title: Restoring a snapshot
docs.text:
To go back to the draft as Builder made it, click Draft created or its Restore button. The dialog closes, and the canvas shows the draft without files-02. Riverside Water is now as you uploaded it, as the other pages expect.

Restoring does not delete the newer snapshots. You can restore them the same way. If the server does not move the draft to the snapshot, for example while you are offline, the page says so, and the draft does not change.

Undo and Redo also move the current snapshot, one change at a time (see Undo and redo).

Warning

A change after you restore or undo removes all newer snapshots, also the snapshots of other users. In the example, a note added after the restore removes "Added device" and "Updated device files-02".

docs.title: Newer snapshots
docs.text:
While the draft shows a snapshot older than its newest one, a notice above the toolbar shows what your next change removes. For example: "Your next change removes 2 newer snapshots (latest by bob, Oct 26, 2026, 10:00 AM)." The notice has two buttons:

  • Return to latest: shows the newest snapshot again. After Undo, it works as Redo and keeps your undo steps. Otherwise, it restores the newest snapshot.
  • Save newer history as a new draft: makes a new draft of the newest snapshot, for example "Riverside Water (copy)". You stay on this draft. The new draft is not published, and its publish makes a new topology, as for Duplicate draft.

The notice closes when your next change removes the newer snapshots, or when the draft shows its newest snapshot again. It does not show while a save conflict is open.

docs.title: Deleting a snapshot
docs.text:
1. Click the Delete button of the snapshot.
  2. Click Delete snapshot. You cannot undo this.

Undo and Redo skip a deleted snapshot.

docs.title: Automatic snapshots
docs.text: When you leave, publish or download a draft with Inspector changes that you did not apply, Builder applies and saves them. Their snapshot has the name of the node, for example "Saved unapplied changes to Device web-01", and the mark Automatic.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
The server holds at most 2,000 drafts of all users. At that limit, it refuses new drafts. To make space, delete drafts, or click Clean up… in Settings. It deletes the published, unchanged drafts of all users (see Cleaning up storage).

A draft keeps at most 50 snapshots and 50 MiB of them. Past either limit, Builder deletes the oldest snapshots. A published diagram and a diagram read from a file have no draft history. To keep one, edit the diagram as a draft.

docs.title: Published diagrams
docs.text:
The Published Diagrams tab lists each topology that has a Builder diagram, by topology name. A topology published from Builder shows its publish time.

Open on a card shows the diagram read only:

To change it, click Edit as a draft. Builder makes a new draft from the published diagram and opens it. The next time any Builder user does this, Builder opens a draft that published the diagram or was made from it, and does not make another. This draft can publish to the topology again (see Publishing again).

A published diagram records who made it and who edited it last. This information comes from the draft at publish time.

docs.title: Opening the experiment
docs.text:
When a diagram was published with an experiment (see Publishing a topology and an experiment), its card and the editor toolbar have Exp. Exp, and Open experiment in the command palette, open the experiment page in the same tab and leave the editor.

Exp shows only while the experiment exists and your role has experiments get on it. It follows a renamed experiment. It does not show for an experiment that you made from the topology yourself. When one publication made several experiments, Exp opens one of them. The others are on the Experiments page.

docs.title: Diagrams read from a file
docs.text:
A topology can name a Builder file on the phenix server as its diagram, without a publish. An administrator sets this up (see Builder documents in files). Its card has the tag File and the file path, but no Delete. To delete the topology, use the Configs page.

Open reads the file and shows its diagram read only. When the stored topology is not what the diagram in the file publishes, the notice says so. Then a draft made from that diagram can publish only as a new topology.

Edit as a draft makes a draft from the diagram in the file. Next time, it opens the same draft while the file has the same diagram. After the file changes, it makes a new draft. Such a draft can update the topology (see Publishing to a topology that names a Builder file).

When phenix cannot use the file, the diagram does not open, and the page says why (see When the file cannot be used). When the file changes between Open and Edit as a draft, Builder makes no draft. Open the diagram again.

docs.title: Deleting a published topology
docs.text:
Delete on a Published Diagrams card deletes the Topology config from phenix. It needs configs delete on the topology. Drafts and experiments made from the topology do not change.

  1. Click Delete on the card.
  2. Click Delete topology.

When another user published or changed the topology after Builder read the list, Builder deletes nothing and reads the list again. Examine the topology, and delete it again.

A draft that published the topology, was imported from it, or was opened from its published diagram creates the topology again the next time it publishes to that name.

docs.title: The Layers tab
docs.text:
A layer set is a named list of layers and its options (see Layers). The Layers tab lists the layer set library of the server, which all users share. On the drafts page, Show Layers in the command palette opens the tab. In a diagram, Edit layers… applies a copy of a set to the diagram.

New layer set opens the layers editor on a new set with the 7 placeholder layers. Upload layer set… adds a set from a layer set file. The tab also has Filter layer sets (see Filtering the lists) and a row to select several sets.

On the cards, the tag Default marks the default set. The tag Built-in marks a set that is part of phenix.

Each card has these buttons (see Item buttons):

  • Edit opens the layers editor. Change the Name, Description, Icon, options and layers, then click Save. Save first writes the text that you typed in the layer rows. When a layer field has an error, the editor stays open and moves focus to that field (see Editing the layers). Each save gives the set its next version. When you made changes, Cancel asks first.
  • Duplicate adds a copy with a number after its name, for example "Purdue Model (2)".
  • Download saves the set as a layer set file.
  • Delete asks first. Diagrams keep their copies of its layers. You cannot undo this.
  • Set default makes the set the default set of the server. On the default set, the button is Clear default.

When another user changed the set or the default after the tab read the library, Delete, Set default and Clear default change nothing. The tab reads the library again. Examine the set, and try again. When another user saved the set after you opened it, Save fails. Close the editor, and open the set again.

The built-in set Purdue Model has the seven levels of the Purdue model, from L0 Process to L5 Enterprise, each with an icon and a color. It is read only and has no Delete. To change it, duplicate it and change the copy.

The server keeps one default set for all users, and each Builder user can change it. Each Blank diagram starts with a copy of the default set, linked to the set. Without a default set, a new diagram has the placeholder layers. In the template editor, a library template offers the layers of the default set (see The template editor).

When Builder cannot read the library, the tab says why and shows Retry. The tab does not list the sets that the server cannot read, for example sets that a newer phenix version saved. It shows how many there are.

The library holds at most 200 sets, plus the built-in set (see The libraries).

docs.title: Selecting several layer sets
docs.text:
Select all, Download selected and Delete selected work as for drafts (see Selecting several drafts), with these differences:

  • Download selected saves a layer set file for each selected set, also the built-in set.
  • Delete selected asks once for all sets. Diagrams keep their copies of the layers. It does not delete a built-in set, and the question and the summary say so. When only built-in sets are selected, Builder asks nothing and shows the summary.

The keys in Selecting with the keyboard also select layer sets.

docs.title: Duplicating a draft
docs.text:
Duplicate makes a new draft with a copy of the current diagram of a draft, and opens it.

Duplicate draft… in the command palette does the same. In the editor, it copies the open draft after Builder saves its changes. On the drafts page, it asks which draft to copy.

The new draft:

  • Has the name of the draft with "(copy)" at the end. When a draft has that name, the copy is "(copy 2)", "(copy 3)" and so on. A copy of "Pump station (copy)" is "Pump station (copy 2)".
  • Has no Draft History. You are its creator.
  • Is not published, and has no link to a topology or experiment. When you publish it, Builder asks for a new topology name and makes a new topology (see Publishing).
  • Still includes the topologies that the original draft included.

A published diagram that shows read only has no Duplicate. Click Edit as a draft first. When the server refuses the new draft, the page says why, and you stay on the same page.

docs.title: Deleting a draft
docs.text:
1. Click Delete on the draft's card.
  2. Click Delete draft. Builder deletes the draft and its whole history from the server. You cannot undo this.

Deleting a draft does not change the configs that it published. During a publish of the draft, the server holds the delete until the publish is done. It then answers 412 with the new ETag of the draft, and Builder tries the delete again once with that ETag. When another user has the draft open, their next save fails (see Autosave and the save state).

docs.title: Selecting several drafts
docs.text:
A card has a checkbox when one of these actions can act on it:

  • Download selected on Drafts and Published Diagrams.
  • Delete selected on Drafts, and on Published Diagrams for the cards that you can delete.
  • Download selected and Delete selected on Icons, for each icon (see The Icons tab).

The row above the cards has the actions, the number of selected cards, and Select all. Select all selects all cards that have a checkbox, or none. With a filter, it acts on the cards that show (see Filtering the lists).

On Published Diagrams, a topology whose diagram is read from a file has no checkbox. Each tab keeps its own selection.

docs.title: Selecting with the keyboard
docs.text:
The cards of a tab are one stop of the Tab key. Tab moves to the card that you were last on, and the keys below work there.

Key What it does Arrow keys Move to the next or previous card, also to the card above or below Home, End Move to the first or last card Space Select the focused card, or clear it Shift+Space, Shift and an arrow key Select the cards from the card you last selected or cleared to the focused card, also when you cleared that card ⌘A (macOS), Ctrl+A Select every card Escape Clear the selection Delete (Backspace on macOS too) Ask to delete the selected cards, where Delete selected can

When you hold Shift and select a checkbox, the cards from the card that you last selected or cleared to that checkbox get its new state. After Select all, ⌘A or Escape, Shift and a checkbox change only that card. Screen readers announce each change of the selection.

docs.title: Downloading several drafts
docs.text:
1. Select the cards.
  2. Click Download selected.

Builder saves a Builder JSON file for each card, one after another, with its custom icons, as Download in the editor does. Each file has the draft as the server has it. Your browser may ask you to let the page download several files. On Published Diagrams, Builder saves each published diagram. The summary under the row lists each card that Builder could not save, with the reason.

docs.title: Deleting several drafts
docs.text:
1. Select the cards of the drafts.
  2. Click Delete selected. Builder asks once for all the drafts.
  3. Click Delete 2 drafts (the number of selected drafts).

On Published Diagrams, Delete selected deletes the topologies of the selected cards. Drafts and experiments made from them do not change.

During the delete, the row shows the progress. When Builder cannot delete some items, the summary under the row lists each with the reason. The failed items stay selected. Dismiss removes the summary.

When the server cannot be reached during a delete or download of several items, Builder stops and lists the remaining items as "Not attempted." Each action uses your permissions for each item.

docs.title: Damaged drafts
docs.text: A draft that this phenix server cannot read stays on the list, for example a draft that a newer phenix version saved. Its card has Delete but no Open. Open the draft with the phenix version that saved it, or delete it. Any Builder user can delete a damaged draft.

docs.title: Logging out
docs.text:
Logging out, or signing in as another user in the same browser, deletes these Builder data from the browser at once: unsent changes, recent commands, the last Auto-group name pattern and the Preflight checks that you last selected. Before you log out, wait until the save state says "All changes saved", or click Download to keep a copy. When your session ends (see Troubleshooting), or after a long time with no activity, phenix logs you out in the same way.

Your preferences stay: the theme, column widths, minimap size, keyboard shortcuts and settings (see Storage).

docs.title: Same draft in multiple tabs
docs.text:
Do not open a draft in more than one tab: Builder can save the changes of only one tab. When a draft is open in more than one tab, each tab shows a notice under the header:

When more than one tab holds unsaved changes, for example after offline work, Builder can save the changes of only one tab. The notice shows how many changes the other tab has. Builder opens the Choose which changes to save dialog:

  1. Under Version to save, choose a version, for example "This tab: 1 change, last at Sep 29, 2026, 1:01:26 PM". Download saves a copy of the version of this tab as a file.
  2. Click Save this version.

Builder saves each other version as a new draft, with " (local copy)" after the name. The tab with that version changes to the new draft. Decide later closes the dialog, and Builder sends nothing until you choose. Choose which to save in the notice opens the dialog again.

docs.title: Draft merging
docs.text:
Another person can save a newer version of the draft before your changes reach the server, for example while you work offline. Builder then merges their changes with yours, field by field. During the merge, edits wait, and the save state says "Merging your changes with the server version…".

  • A change that only one of you made stays, also on different fields of one device. If alice moves router-1 and you rename it, router-1 is moved and renamed.
  • Items that one of you added stay. An item that one of you deleted is deleted, unless the other changed it or added a connection to it.
  • An interface that one of you renamed keeps the changes of the other.
  • Builder adds or deletes the scenarios that one of you added or deleted.
  • Your view of the canvas (zoom and position) does not change.

When nothing clashes, Builder saves the merged diagram on top of the newer version and announces "Merged alice's changes with yours." Draft History lists the save as "Merged changes from alice". Undo goes back to alice's version. Redo brings back the merged diagram.

These changes clash:

  • A field that you both changed to different values. A device's name, its hostname and the hostname in its settings are one choice. The new names of one interface are one choice, and the diagram keeps one interface. The whole link of a linked template is one choice.
  • An item that one of you deleted while the other changed it or added a connection to it. For a device or interface, the choices are, for example, Keep theirs: delete ws-01 and drop your connection to it and Keep mine: keep ws-01 with your connection. Builder announces each connection that it drops.
  • A group that one of you deleted or ungrouped while the other put a node in it. When Builder deletes the group, the node goes to the group that held that group, as Ungroup does, or to no group. Builder announces each node that it moves.
  • A node that one of you put in a group while the other put that group in the node. Two groups cannot be in each other.

For the group of a node, the choices name the groups, for example Keep mine: Site and Keep theirs: no group. If your choices still put two groups in each other, Builder moves one of them out of its group and announces it.

When something clashes, or the merged diagram has an error such as two devices with one hostname, the panel This draft changed on the server opens under the header. Your unsaved changes stay on this device. Builder does not save new edits until you choose one of these:

  • Review and merge: opens the Merge changes from alice dialog.
  • Save my history as a new draft: saves your version as a new draft, for example "Riverside Water (local copy)", and opens it. The draft that changed on the server does not change. If the save stops before it is complete, Builder deletes the incomplete draft and says why.
  • Discard mine and load the server version: asks first, then deletes your changes and loads the newer version. You cannot undo this. If Builder cannot read the newer version, it keeps your changes and says why.

The Merge changes from alice dialog lists each clash with Keep mine and Keep theirs and the value of each:

  • Choose one for each clash, or click Keep all mine or Keep all theirs.
  • Save merged saves the merged diagram on top of the newer version, with all changes that do not clash. If the merged diagram has an error, the dialog lists it and stays open.
  • When the dialog opens only for such an error, Save merged is unavailable. Click Cancel, then save your history as a new draft or discard it.
  • If a newer version arrives when you click Save merged, Builder saves nothing and merges again.
  • If the save fails, the dialog says why and keeps your choices. Click Save merged again.
  • Cancel goes back to the panel.

For example, alice and you both rename ws-01 and change its description:

Merging needs the version that your changes started from. The panel says "Merging is not available" and does not offer Review and merge when:

  • The server no longer keeps that version (a draft keeps its last 50 snapshots).
  • Builder cannot read it.
  • The server does not send it within 15 seconds.

If the merge fails, the panel says "Merging failed" with the reason, and offers the same choices. If a third person saves while Builder saves the merged diagram, Builder merges again with their version.

docs.title: The Editor: details
docs.text:
Info

This page holds every rule, limit and message of this feature. For the short guide, see The Editor.

In the editor, you draw and change a diagram. To open it, see Opening a draft. For tasks such as adding and connecting devices, see Building a Diagram. Checks and Preflight and Command Palette and Shortcuts have their own pages. The examples use the Riverside Water draft of the example lab.

The editor has five areas:

  1. The header: the diagram name, the counts, the checks and the view buttons.
  2. The toolbar: the editing, layout, download and publish buttons, and the save state.
  3. Nodes & Templates, the left column, with Nodes & Objects.
  4. The canvas.
  5. The Inspector, which changes the selection.

docs.title: Header
docs.text:
From left to right, the header holds:

  • Drafts: opens the drafts page. Your changes continue to save.
  • The diagram name. Point at a long name to see all of it.
  • Edit diagram name (the pencil), except in a published diagram (see Renaming the diagram).
  • The resource totals.
  • The counts of devices, switches, networks, connections, groups and notes, and of layers while a device or a switch is at a layer (see Selecting by kind).
  • The checks button, which opens Diagram checks (see Checks and warnings).
  • Reset view (see Canvas).
  • Commands: opens the command palette.
  • The theme button (see Themes).
  • Shortcuts: opens the keyboard shortcuts sheet. The button shows the key that opens the sheet, if there is one.
  • Settings: opens Builder settings.
  • Help: opens this documentation in a new tab.
  • Focus mode: full-screen mode for focused editing (see Focus mode).

In a narrow window, the buttons after the checks button show only their icons. Shortcuts keeps its key.

docs.title: Selecting by kind
docs.text:
Click a count to replace the selection with all items of that kind. Focus stays on the count. For example, 12 devices selects the 12 devices, and Builder announces "Selected 12 devices."

  • The networks count selects the switches of the networks, because the canvas shows each network as its switch.
  • The connections count selects only connections.
  • The layers count includes the placeholder layers. It selects each device and switch that is at a layer: the layer chosen for the node, or the layer that its fields match (see Layers).
  • A count of 0 selects nothing.

To select the nodes of one layer, use Select nodes on layer in the command palette. To select the devices on one network, or the devices that use one disk image, use Select devices on network or Select devices using image.

The counts are one Tab stop. The arrow keys, Home and End move between them.

docs.title: Resource totals
docs.text:
The totals add the vCPUs and the memory of each device that phenix starts, as a VM or as a container. An external device does not count. A device from an included topology counts, because the experiment starts it too. A device with no vCPUs or Memory, or with a value that is not a whole number above 0, counts as 1 vCPU and 512 MB, as phenix starts it. Memory shows in MB below 1 GB, else in GB (1 GB is 1024 MB).

When the selection holds devices, the totals of the selection show below, for example "Selected: 2 vCPUs, 1 GB RAM". A device in a selected group counts one time. The totals do not show when the diagram has no device that phenix starts. In a narrow window, the vCPUs and the memory show on two lines, and the totals of the selection do not show.

To compare the totals with the free resources of the cluster, run the Host capacity check of Preflight.

docs.title: Renaming the diagram
docs.text:
1. Click Edit diagram name. A field replaces the name, with the name selected.
  2. Type the new name.
  3. Press Enter, or move focus out of the field.

Esc keeps the old name. Undo restores the old name. The Name field of the Inspector changes the same name. The topology name is different: you choose it when you publish (see Publishing).

docs.title: Toolbar
docs.text:
Button Function More Undo, Redo Undo or redo the last change. After an undo, a notice says how many newer snapshots your next change removes. Undo and redo, Newer snapshots Copy, Paste Copy the selection, or paste a copy of it. Copy, paste, duplicate and delete Delete Delete the selected nodes and connections. Copy, paste, duplicate and delete Group, Ungroup Put the selected nodes in a new group, or remove a selected group and keep its nodes. Groups Auto-group A menu: By network, By name or By name pattern…. Auto-group Layout menu Arrange the diagram. The menu shows the layout of the draft, or Default when no layout ran. Layouts Scenarios Choose, view, edit or create the scenarios of the diagram, or store a scenario file on the server. Scenarios Download Save the diagram as a file. Downloading Upload Open a Builder document, a published diagram or a legacy Builder diagram as a new draft. Import, Upload and Download Publish Write Topology and Experiment configs, and add the topology to the scenarios of the diagram. Publishing Exp Open the experiment that you published the diagram with. It shows only while that experiment exists and your role can read it. Opening the experiment Minimap Show or hide the minimap. Canvas Draft History List the snapshots of the draft, and restore one. Draft History

The save state follows, for example "All changes saved". When a save fails, Retry saving follows it (see How drafts save).

A button that does not apply is unavailable, for example Ungroup while the selection holds no group. In a published diagram, the editing buttons are unavailable.

The tooltip of a button shows its keys. The keys in the tooltips of the layout menu and Auto-group run Auto layout and Auto-group by network without the menu.

docs.title: Actions that take time
docs.text: A button whose action can take time, such as Publish, shows a turning ring while the action runs. The button keeps its name, its size and focus. A second press does nothing. A dialog also says what it does, for example "Preparing PNG…". With reduced motion, the ring does not turn.

docs.title: Canvas
docs.text:
• Select: click a node or a connection. Shift-click adds a node to the selection, or removes it. Click an empty spot to clear the selection.
  • Move: drag a node. A drag of a group moves its nodes. With Snap to grid on in Settings, nodes go to the grid of the diagram (see Grid size in With nothing selected).
  • Move with keys: Shift and an arrow key move the selected nodes 10 pixels, without the grid. Builder saves the move as one undo step when you release the key or focus leaves the canvas (see Arranging by hand).
  • Pan: drag an empty spot.
  • Zoom: use the mouse wheel, or Zoom in, Zoom out and Fit diagram to view at the bottom left. After a fit, the third button is Restore previous view.
  • Connect: drag from the connection point of a device to a switch (see Connecting interfaces).
  • Edit: double-click a node to open the Node Editor. A double-click on a line adds a bend.

A press is a click, not a drag, while the pointer stays within 4 screen pixels at any zoom, or 8 pixels with a finger or a pen. A click selects the node and does not move it. When Builder cannot accept a move, for example while a save conflict is open, the nodes return to their old positions.

A device shows its icon, hostname, Type, number of interfaces and description. An external device shows External, and a device with no type shows Device. A device from an included topology has a dashed border, and shows its source in place of its type (see Included topologies). A node with an issue has a mark at its top left corner (see Checks and warnings).

A switch shows its icon and the name of its network. Its outline has the color of its network connections, unless the switch has its own outline color or the color of its layer. An icon has the color of the outline of its node. A device with no outline color shows its icon in the accent color of the theme (see Colors).

The minimap at the bottom right shows the full diagram. To resize it, drag Resize minimap at its top left corner. Minimap in the toolbar shows or hides it until the next diagram opens.

With Show coordinates on in Settings, rulers show X and Y in canvas pixels, and a band shows the extent of the selected nodes. For a node in a group, Position starts at the top left corner of the group, so it does not agree with the rulers. PNG and SVG downloads do not show the rulers.

To hide the connections on your canvas only, see Hiding connections. For the canvas keys, see Keys on the canvas.

Reset view in the header does not change the diagram. It does these steps:

  • It resets the zoom to Zoom when a diagram opens in Settings: 100%, the full diagram, or your custom percentage.
  • It shows the minimap at its default size, unless Settings turn it off.
  • It shows both side columns at their default widths.
  • It closes the sections that you opened, such as More settings, and expands the sections that you collapsed (see Collapsing sections).
  • It scrolls the columns to the top.

docs.title: Info tooltips
docs.text:
Rest the pointer on a device or a switch, or move focus to it, to see its info tooltip:

Node Rows of the tooltip Device Description, cut to 80 characters. Interfaces: each interface with its address, for example "eth0 — 10.10.20.101/24", or "DHCP". OS type. Switch Network: the name of the network. VLAN alias, or "no alias". Description, cut to 80 characters. Connected devices, with their number: each device on this switch, with the address of its interface.

A list shows its first 8 entries, then "+N more". An empty row says "None", and a device with no OS type says "Not set".

The tooltip stays while the pointer is on the node or the tooltip, and while the node has focus. While a node has focus, the pointer on another node shows the tooltip of that node. Esc closes the tooltip until focus moves, and keeps the selection. Screen readers read the same facts as the description of the node. Notes, groups, drawings and connections have no tooltip, and PNG and SVG downloads do not show it.

docs.title: Side columns
docs.text:
Nodes & Templates is the left column, and the Inspector is the right column. Each column has two toggles:

  • Widen Nodes & Templates and Widen Inspector make the column as wide as possible. Click the toggle again to restore the width.
  • Hide Nodes & Templates and Hide Inspector fold the column into a narrow strip. The strip holds the toggle that shows the column.

To set a width, drag the splitter (Resize Nodes & Templates, Resize Inspector). Double-click it to restore the default width. A selection on the canvas shows a hidden Inspector. The browser keeps the widths and the hidden columns.

In a window narrower than about 900 pixels, or at a high browser zoom, the columns stack, and the page scrolls.

docs.title: Nodes & Objects
docs.text:
Nodes & Objects lists Device, Switch, Note, Group, and the drawings Rectangle, Circle, Icon and Line (see Shapes, icons and lines). Under Templates, it lists the device templates in sections. Click an item to add it, or drag it onto the canvas. Builder puts the new node in free space and selects it. Point at an item to see its description. See Adding devices.

For the template sections, the template buttons and the updates of linked templates, see Templates in the editor and Linked templates.

To find a node, use Go to node in the command palette (type @). To find a network, use Go to network (type #). To rename a node, select it and press F2: focus goes to its name in the Inspector. Remove network in the command palette removes a network and its switches, also a network that no switch shows (see Adding switches and networks).

docs.title: Inspector
docs.text:
The Inspector shows and changes the fields of one selected node or connection. With nothing selected, or with several items selected, it shows the diagram.

A text box for more than one line, such as Description, grows with its text to eight lines, then scrolls. To make it taller, drag its bottom right corner.

docs.title: The Inspector header
docs.text:
When you select one node, the header names it, for example "Device edge-rtr". It has three buttons:

  • Add connection: opens Add a connection, which connects a device to a switch without a drag (see Add a connection without dragging). It shows for a device or a switch, but not for a device from an included topology.
  • Move to group: opens Move to a group, which puts the node in a group, or removes it from its group (see Groups).
  • Open Node Editor (the pencil): opens the Node Editor.

Each dialog starts from the selection. The tooltip of each button shows its name and keys. Add connection and Move to group have no keys until you set some (see Customizing shortcuts). A published diagram shows only Open Node Editor.

docs.title: Collapsing sections
docs.text:
A group of fields (such as General or Hardware), a list (such as Interfaces or Drives) and each list entry (such as "Interface 1: eth0") can collapse. Click its name to collapse or expand it. A collapsed entry keeps its buttons to move, insert and remove it.

  • A collapsed part that holds a field with an error shows a cross after its name. Screen readers read "has errors".
  • A collapsed section expands when you go to one of its fields, or when Apply or Save now stops because of an error in it.
  • The sections stay collapsed for the next node until you leave the page. The Inspector, the Node Editor and the template editor each keep their own collapsed sections.
  • Reset view expands all sections and entries.
  • A search in the Node Editor expands the sections with a match until the search ends (see Searching the fields).

Point at the label of a field to see its help. For a field of the phenix spec, the help starts with its topology YAML path, for example hardware.vcpus.

docs.title: With nothing selected
docs.text:
The Diagram section has these fields. A published diagram shows them as text.

  • Name and Description. Click Apply to keep a change.
  • Template updates: shows only when a linked template of the diagram needs attention. It has Update, Update all or Unlink, but no buttons in a published diagram (see Linked templates).
  • Icon size: Small, Medium or Large (see Icon size). While your Node icon size setting is not Off, a note says that the setting overrides this size on your canvas. The diagram keeps its size.
  • Grid size: the spacing of the canvas grid in pixels, 16 by default. Type a whole number from 4 to 200, then press Enter or leave the field. Other values show an error and change nothing. Nodes go to the grid only while Snap to grid is on in Settings.
  • Layers: the list of layers, or a note that the diagram has the 7 placeholder layers (see Layers). For layers from a layer set, a line names the set and its version. When the set has a newer version, Update from layer set copies it into the diagram. Edit layers… opens the layers editor. A published diagram shows neither button.

  • Details, read only. A row shows only when the diagram has its value:

    • Created: the time and the user that made the diagram.
    • Last edited: when the server saved the content that you see, and by whom. After Undo or Restore, it shows the save of the earlier version.
    • Source file: the file of an Upload, or the config file of an Import.

    See Who made and last saved a diagram. - Annotations: for a draft imported from a config, the annotations of that config. You cannot change them, and publishing does not write them (see What an import keeps). - Notes: text about the full diagram, one box for each note. Add note adds a box. Builder saves a note when you leave its box. To remove a note, empty its box, or click its Delete button. Builder JSON and YAML keep the notes, but publishing writes them to no config. - Scenarios: "No scenarios." and Add scenario, or a sub-heading for each scenario, for example "Scenario riverside-water (2 apps, 6 hosts)". Edit scenarios opens the Scenarios dialog (see Scenarios).

A diagram holds at most 100 notes of at most 4096 bytes each, in UTF-8. At 100 notes, Add note is unavailable. Builder does not save a note that is too long, or that holds a control character other than a line break or a tab. It shows an error under the box.

The app count of a scenario includes the disabled apps, and a host counts one time. A scenario with disabled apps adds their number, for example "1 disabled app". Under the sub-heading, each app shows its hosts. An app with no hosts shows "(no hosts)", and a disabled app shows "(disabled)". To read the apps, Builder needs configs get on the scenario. Without it, the Inspector says that it cannot read them.

docs.title: Editing a node
docs.text:
Select a node to see its fields. A device has these sections:

  • Hostname, Icon, Icon size, Outline Color and Fill Color (see The Icon field, Colors and Icon size). While your Node icon size setting is not Off, Icon size has a note that the setting overrides it on your canvas.
  • Node: the fields of the phenix spec of the node. These are Type, and General (Description, Do not boot, Node hostname, Snapshot, VM type).
  • Hardware: CPU, Drives (Image and more for each drive), Memory, OS type and VCPUs.
  • Network: Interfaces, OSPF, Routes and Firewall rulesets.
  • More settings, a bar that you click to open: miniccc commands, Delay, Injections, Advanced settings, Labels and Annotations.
  • Layer: the layer of the device (see Layers). A device with no chosen layer can be at the layer that its fields match. Use matched layer removes the chosen layer. Edit layers… opens the layers editor.
  • Connection points: the interfaces of the device, each with a connection point on the canvas.
  • Position: X and Y, and Move.

A field marked * must have a value. An empty optional field shows the value that phenix uses, for example "Default (kvm)" for VM type. A field that holds a value other than its default shows a Default button. Default empties an optional field, or gives a required field its default value. Click Apply to keep the change.

Some fields do not accept all values:

  • A list of choices with a value that is not a choice, as in an uploaded topology, shows that value with "(not one of the choices)" and a warning.
  • A number field shows an error for text that is not a number. A field for a whole number also shows an error for a number such as 1.5 or 1e3.
  • Memory and VCPUs can hold template text, such as {{ .Memory }}, until you type a number.

To change fields:

  1. Change one or more fields. A bar at the bottom shows "Unapplied changes", with Apply and Cancel.
  2. Click Apply, or press Enter in a field. Builder changes the diagram and saves it.

Cancel discards the changes. While a changed field has an error, Apply is unavailable. When the diagram changes while you edit, the Inspector keeps your unapplied changes.

When you select another node, the Inspector applies valid changes and discards changes that are not valid. Builder also saves unapplied changes when you leave, publish or download the draft (see Automatic snapshots).

These changes take effect at once, without Apply:

  • The fields in Fields that take effect at once.
  • Layer.
  • Show description on the canvas (see Hiding descriptions on the canvas).
  • An addition, disconnection or removal of a connection point.

The fields come from the phenix server. When the server cannot send them, the Inspector says so, and shows the fields built into Builder. These may differ from what this server accepts (see Permissions).

docs.title: Other kinds of nodes
docs.text:
• A switch is one network. Its Inspector ("Network CORP") has Name, VLAN alias, Subnet, Gateway, Description, Edge Color, Line style, Outline Color, Fill Color, Icon size, Layer, Addresses and Position (see Adding switches and networks and Addresses of a network). Layer takes effect at once, as on a device.
  • A note has Text, Color and Position (see Notes).
  • A group has Title, Description, Color, Border pattern, Icon, Icon size and Position (see Groups).
  • A connection has Label (by default, the name of the network), Color and Line style. Its Inspector names it, for example "Connection from ntp-01 (eth0) to CORP".
  • A rectangle or a circle has Shape, Label, Fill Color, Outline Color, Border pattern, Width and Height.
  • An icon has Icon, Label, Width and Height.
  • A line has Label, Color, Line style, Arrowhead at the start, Arrowhead at the end and Points, with X and Y for each point (see Shapes, icons and lines).

docs.title: Addresses of a network
docs.text:
The Inspector of a switch has these fields for the addresses of its network. Publishing does not write them to the topology.

  • Subnet: the IPv4 network, for example 10.10.20.0/24.
  • Gateway: the IPv4 address of the router on the network. It must be in the subnet.

Assign addresses, under Addresses, gives each static interface on the network that has no address the next free address of the subnet. The change is one step of Undo, for example "Assigned 3 addresses on network CORP". The button uses the applied Subnet. When the network has no subnet, the button is unavailable. Assign addresses in the command palette does the same for a network that you choose.

For how Builder gives addresses and gateways, and what it announces, see Subnets and addresses.

docs.title: Fields that take effect at once
docs.text:
These fields change how a node or a connection looks:

Where Fields that take effect at once Device Icon, Icon size, Outline Color, Fill Color Switch Edge Color, Line style, Outline Color, Fill Color, Icon size Group Color, Border pattern, Icon, Icon size Note Color Rectangle or circle Fill Color, Outline Color, Border pattern Icon Icon Line Label, Color, Line style Connection Label, Color, Line style

Each change is one step of Undo, for example "Changed the fill color of Device web-01 to #2f6fbf". A text field, such as Label, takes effect when you press Enter or move focus out of the field. Before that, Esc restores the text that the field had. In the template editor, these fields change the template at once, and Save saves the template.

docs.title: Hiding descriptions on the canvas
docs.text:
A device and a group show their Description on the canvas. To hide it for one node, click the eye button (Show description on the canvas) beside Description. The button is on while the canvas shows the description. The change takes effect at once, and is one step of Undo, for example "Hid the description of Device web-01 on the canvas". The template editor and the Node Editor have the same button. The diagram keeps the choice.

The node keeps its description, and the info tooltip still shows it. PNG, SVG and draw.io downloads do not show it. Publish and the checks do not change.

To hide the descriptions of all nodes on your canvas, disable Show node descriptions in Settings, or choose Hide node descriptions in the command palette. While the setting is off, each Description field says "Your canvas shows no descriptions, because your Show node descriptions setting is off."

docs.title: The Icon field
docs.text:
Icon shows the icon of the node and its name. To change the icon:

  1. Click Icon, or move focus to it and press ↓. The list of built-in icons opens, with focus on the icon in use.
  2. Select an icon. To go to an icon, type its first letter.

Default, at the start of the list, is the icon of the node when it has no icon of its own. An icon drawing has no Default. At the end of the list, Custom icon… opens the Custom icons dialog (see Custom icons). In a published diagram, the list does not open.

docs.title: Fields you cannot change
docs.text:
• A device from an included topology is read only, and the Inspector says so. You can still move it. Combine into a new draft makes a copy of the diagram in which the included devices are its own (see Making included devices editable).
  • You cannot rename a network that an included device is on. Its other fields can change.
  • All fields are read only in a published diagram (see Published diagrams).

docs.title: Node Editor
docs.text:
The Node Editor shows the fields of one node in a large dialog, in columns. To open it, do one of these steps:

  • Select the node, then click Open Node Editor in the Inspector header.
  • Double-click the node on the canvas.
  • Select the node, or move focus to it on the canvas. Then press ⌥+⇧+E on macOS, or Alt+Shift+E on Windows and Linux.
  • In the command palette, select Open Node Editor. With no single node selected, the palette asks for a device or a switch.

The Node Editor has the fields that the Inspector shows, and the checks of the node. Edit layers… opens the layers editor over the Node Editor, which keeps your changes. The first field has focus.

docs.title: Sections and the table of contents
docs.text:
The Node Editor has these tools. Expand all, Collapse all and the table of contents show only for a device.

  • Search fields shows only the fields that match (see Searching the fields).
  • Expand all and Collapse all expand or collapse all sections and entries (see Collapsing sections).
  • The table of contents lists the sections, their lists and entries, Connection points, Position, and Checks when the node has issues. A list shows its number of entries. An entry with a field error shows a cross. Click an entry to expand it, scroll to it and move focus to it. The table of contents marks the entry in view. During a search, it lists only the parts that the search shows.
  • In a window narrower than 900 pixels, click Table of contents to show it above the fields. A choice in it closes it again.

The section headers stay at the top while you scroll.

docs.title: Searching the fields
docs.text:
Search fields finds a field by its label, such as memory, or by its path in the topology YAML, such as network.interfaces[0].vlan. A part of a path also matches, for example interfaces.vlan. The search ignores letter case and field values. With two or more words, each word must match.

  • Only the matching fields show, and their sections expand. A section, list or entry whose name matches shows all its fields.
  • A line under the box counts the matches.
  • To show all fields again, empty the box, or press Esc in it. When the box is empty, Esc closes the Node Editor.
  • When Apply stops because of errors, the search empties. The sections stay expanded, so you can see the fields with errors.

To edit a node in the Node Editor:

  1. Change one or more fields.
  2. Click Apply. Builder applies all changes as one step of Undo, closes the Node Editor and moves focus to the node on the canvas.

Cancel, Esc and Close dialog close the Node Editor. If you did not apply your changes, Builder asks you to discard them or keep editing.

The changes that take effect at once in the Inspector also do so here: Fields that take effect at once, Layer, Connection points and Move. Cancel does not discard them. Use Undo.

Before the Node Editor opens, the Inspector applies its unapplied changes. If one of them has an error, the Node Editor does not open. When you leave or reload the draft, Builder applies and saves the unapplied changes of the Node Editor.

In a published diagram, the Node Editor is read only and has only Close. The fields of a device from an included topology are also read only.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
To open Builder settings, click Settings in the header, or press ⌥+⇧+S on macOS or Alt+Shift+S on Windows and Linux. This works in the editor and on the drafts page. Changes apply at once, and the browser keeps them after you log out. They do not change the diagram.

Group Setting Default Function Appearance Theme System System, Light or Dark (see Themes). Appearance Reduce motion Off The canvas pans and zooms at once, and nothing moves. Motion is also reduced when your device asks for it. Canvas Default layout ELK layered The layout that Auto layout and Auto-group use on a draft whose layout menu says Default. The draft then keeps it. A change moves no node (see Layouts). Canvas Show the minimap On Shows the minimap when a diagram opens. Canvas Show node icons On Shows the icons of devices, switches and groups on the canvas and in PNG, SVG and draw.io downloads. Canvas Show node descriptions On Shows the descriptions of devices and groups on the canvas and in PNG, SVG and draw.io downloads (see Hiding descriptions on the canvas). Canvas Show connections On Shows the connections on your canvas (see Hiding connections). Canvas Node icon size Off Off uses the icon sizes of the diagram. Small, Medium or Large replaces them on your canvas and in your PNG, SVG and draw.io downloads. Other users see the sizes of the diagram. Canvas Show coordinates Off Shows X and Y rulers on the canvas (see Canvas). Canvas Zoom when a diagram opens 100% 100%, Fit the whole diagram in view, or Custom with a percentage from 20 to 200. Builder rounds it to a multiple of 5. A number out of range shows an error. Reset view also uses this zoom. Editing Snap to grid Off Nodes that you drag or drop, new nodes and the points of lines go to the grid of the diagram. See Grid size in With nothing selected. Editing Assign addresses on connect On A static interface with no address that you connect, paste or duplicate gets the next free address of the subnet (see Addresses of a network). Keyboard Single-key shortcuts On See Single-key shortcuts. Keyboard Change keyboard shortcuts See Customizing shortcuts. Layers Edit layers… In the editor, opens the layers editor. On the drafts page, shows the Layers tab (see The drafts page). The layers of a diagram are not a setting. Storage Clean up… Deletes the published, unchanged drafts of all users, and the stored data that nothing uses (see Cleaning up storage).

Commands of the same names in the command palette change Show node icons, Show node descriptions, Show connections, Node icon size and Snap to grid.

Clean up… shows what it would delete, and asks before it deletes:

  • It first saves the open draft.
  • It deletes nothing when that save fails.
  • It deletes nothing when a draft that it would delete has changes on this device that the server does not have.
  • If it deletes the open draft, Builder does not save your next change. To keep a copy, click Download first.

Reset to defaults resets all settings, but not the layers of a diagram, the default layer set or your shortcut keys.

docs.title: Layers editor
docs.text:
The layers editor, Layers of this diagram, changes the layers of the open diagram. To open it, select Edit layers… in one of these places:

  • The Inspector, under Layers with nothing selected, or beside the Layer of a device or a switch.
  • The Node Editor, beside Layer. The layers editor opens over the Node Editor, which keeps your unapplied changes.
  • Builder settings.
  • The command palette.

Each change is one step of Undo. A diagram with the placeholder layers saves them with your first change. In a published diagram, the layers editor is read only. For its parts, see Editing the layers.

docs.title: Focus mode
docs.text:
Focus mode hides the phenix navigation bar, so Builder fills the window. Click Focus mode in the header, or press ⇧+⌘+F (Ctrl+Shift+F). To end it, click Exit focus mode or press the same keys.

Focus mode also asks the browser for full screen:

  • If the browser refuses full screen, focus mode fills the window only.
  • When you leave full screen from the browser, focus mode stays on in the window.
  • Focus mode stays on between the drafts page and the editor.
  • Focus mode ends when you use its button or its keys, or leave Builder. Ending focus mode also leaves full screen.

docs.title: Themes
docs.text:
The theme button in the header shows the theme in use: System, Light or Dark. System follows the light or dark appearance of your device. Each press selects the next theme. On a device with a light appearance, the order is System, Dark, Light. On a dark one, it is System, Light, Dark. Theme in Settings sets the same choice.

The theme changes only Builder, not the rest of phenix. PNG and SVG downloads use the background of the theme in use. A draw.io download always has the colors of the light theme.

docs.title: Accessibility
docs.text:
You can use Builder with only a keyboard, and with a screen reader.

  • From the top of the page, press Tab to reach Skip to diagram canvas.
  • The diagram, the toolbar and the header counts are each one Tab stop (see Keys on the canvas). The arrow keys, Home and End move between the toolbar buttons. With a screen reader, use its focus mode (forms mode in JAWS) for the canvas keys.
  • A custom icon is decoration. It does not change the screen reader text of a node.
  • To add and connect nodes without a pointer, use Nodes & Objects and the Inspector header. In the command palette, type connect or group to open the same dialogs. To find a node, use Go to node. Esc closes a dialog and returns focus to where you opened it.
  • Builder announces the result of each change, for example "Updated device ws-01.", and each setting change from the command palette.
  • A field that suggests values, such as the Image of a drive, announces the number of matching suggestions.
  • An open dialog announces what its changes did. Builder announces the other messages when the dialog closes.

Builder aims to meet WCAG 2.2 level AA.

docs.title: Icons: details
docs.text:
Info

This page holds every rule, limit and message of this feature. For the short guide, see Templates and Icons.

docs.title: Built-in icons
docs.text:
Devices, groups and icon drawings show a built-in icon, which you select under Icon in the Inspector. The icon is only a picture: it does not change the phenix settings of a device. A device made from a template gets the template's icon.

Kind Icons Computers Server (any virtual machine, and the default for a device), Desktop, Laptop, Smartphone, Printer, NTP Server Networks Router, Switch, Firewall, VLAN, Container (the default for a group), External device (hardware in the loop) Industrial control PLC, RTU, RTAC (an automation controller or a data gateway), Relay, Transmission, Distribution, Cell Tower Operating systems Linux, CentOS, Red Hat, Ubuntu, Fedora, openSUSE, Alpine, Kali Linux, BSD, Windows, Apple, Android Tools Terminal, pfSense, Wireshark, Zeek (a network sensor) People and roles Hacker (an attacker), Black Hat (a threat actor), Human, Robot (a bot or a script) Other roles Lizard and Fox, for a role with no other icon, such as a team mascot Servers phēnix, minimega

To preview a built-in icon, or to download it as a PNG file, use the Icons tab.

Names and logos of products are trademarks of their owners. phenix is not affiliated with or endorsed by them. The icon notices give the source and the license of each icon that comes from another work.

docs.title: Icon size
docs.text:
Devices, switches and groups draw their icons at Small (16 pixels), Medium (24 pixels) or Large (32 pixels). Set the size for the whole diagram under Icon size in the Diagram section of the Inspector (select an empty part of the canvas). A new diagram draws Small icons.

A device, a switch or a group can have its own size. Its Icon size offers the three sizes and Diagram default, which names the diagram's size, for example "Diagram default (Large)". Both fields take effect at once.

Nodes keep their size on the canvas. Text that does not fit ends with an ellipsis. The Inspector and the node's tooltip show all of it. PNG, SVG and draw.io downloads draw the icons at their sizes.

docs.title: Your own icon size and hidden icons
docs.text:
Two settings in the Canvas section of Settings change how your canvas draws icons. They do not change the diagram, and other users do not see them. This browser keeps them.

  • Node icon size: Off (the default), Small, Medium or Large. A size other than Off draws each node icon at that size, on your canvas and in PNG, SVG and draw.io downloads. The diagram, its history and its files keep their own sizes. While the setting is not Off, each Icon size field says, for example, "Your Node icon size setting (Large) overrides this on your canvas." The command palette has a Node icon size: command for each value.
  • Show node icons: on by default. When it is off, devices, switches and groups show no icon on the canvas and in PNG, SVG and draw.io downloads, and their text uses all the width. Show or hide node icons in the command palette changes the setting.

docs.title: Custom icons
docs.text:
A device, a group or an icon drawing can show an image of your own in place of its built-in icon. A switch and a note cannot. All users of the server share one icon library of at most 2,000 custom icons. The built-in icons do not count against this limit. Use the Icons tab, the editor or the REST API to manage the library.

To choose a custom icon:

  1. Select the device, the group or the icon.
  2. In the Inspector, click Icon.
  3. At the end of the list, select Custom icon….
  4. In the Custom icons dialog, click Upload icon… and choose an image file, or click Use on a listed icon.

Icon then shows the image and its name, followed by "(custom icon)". The change takes effect at once. To use a built-in icon again, select it in the list.

A node stores the name of its custom icon, and shows the server's icon of that name. When the server has no icon of that name, Icon adds "(custom icon not found: the node shows its built-in icon)". This occurs when someone deleted the icon, or the diagram came from another server. The node shows its built-in icon until someone uploads an icon of that name.

Until Builder reads the image of an icon, the node shows an empty square of the icon's size.

The dialog lists:

  • In this diagram: copies of icons that the diagram holds from an uploaded file (see The diagram and its icons). Each has Use, and Add to server when the server does not have it. "On the server" marks a copy that the server has.
  • Server icons: each icon on the server, with its uploader, its size and its other names, and the library count, for example "The library holds 2 of 2000 icons." Filter icons filters by name, other name or uploader. Each icon has Use, and Rename when a user uploaded it.

docs.title: The Icons tab
docs.text:
The Icons tab of the drafts page shows the built-in icons and each icon on the server. To open it, select Show Icons in the command palette. To open the preview of one icon, type i: and part of its name (see Command palette).

Show selects Built-in icons (the default) or Server icons. An upload, or a preview from i:, sets it to Server icons. The count, for example "The library holds 45 of 2000 icons.", includes the built-in icons. Filter icons filters by name, other name or uploader.

With Server icons, each icon on the server has a card with its size and source. The source is "Uploaded by" and the user, or "Server" for an icon from a template file. A card has a checkbox, View, Download, and Delete when a user uploaded the icon.

View shows the icon at its stored size, at most 96 by 96 pixels, and at 16, 24 and 32 pixels.

Download saves the icon as a PNG file, exactly as the server stores it, with the name of the icon, for example plc.png. Download selected saves one PNG file for each selected icon, built-in icons included.

Delete and Delete selected ask first (see Renaming and deleting icons). The cards use the keys of the other tabs (see Selecting several drafts). Filter icons limits what Select all selects. A change of Show clears the selection.

Delete selected deletes only icons that a user uploaded. Its question also counts the others, for example "1 other selected icon cannot be deleted." When no selected icon can be deleted, it asks nothing. A summary under the selection row gives the reason for each icon that it could not download or delete. An icon that the server no longer has leaves the list, and the summary lists it.

When Builder cannot read the library, the tab says "Could not load the server's icons." and why, with Retry.

docs.title: Built-in icons in the Icons tab
docs.text:
With Built-in icons, the cards are in the order of the table in Built-in icons. Filter icons filters them by name, key or the word "Built-in". Each card shows the key that a diagram stores, for example "Key: router".

A built-in icon has a checkbox, View and Download. You cannot delete or rename it. Download saves a PNG file of 96 by 96 pixels, named after the key, for example router.png. The browser makes the file from the icon's drawing: a dark icon on a clear background, for use on a light background.

docs.title: Uploading an icon
docs.text:
Upload icon… takes a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG file of at most 5 MiB. The browser converts it to a PNG of at most 96 by 96 pixels, in the picture's own proportions. It does not enlarge a small picture, and it draws an SVG as large as an icon can be. The dialog then asks for the icon's name, proposed from the file name. Add icon uploads the icon.

A name is 1 to 64 letters, digits, _, @, . or -. It is unique on the server, ignoring case, and the first upload of a name keeps it. The server refuses a name that it has for another image, and names the uploader, for example "icon name "plc" belongs to an icon alice uploaded. Choose another name". When you upload the same image under its own name again, the dialog says "The server already has this icon as" and its name.

Builder does not load style sheets, images or fonts from outside an SVG file, so those parts are missing from the icon. When the SVG cannot be converted, the dialog says "The Builder could not convert this image. Save it as a PNG, and then upload it again."

A custom icon keeps its own colors in the light and the dark theme. Choose an icon that is clear on both, or give the node a Fill Color.

docs.title: The diagram and its icons
docs.text:
A draft names its icons. Except in the cases below, it holds no image of them, so a saved draft stays small. A Builder JSON or YAML download holds a copy of each icon that the diagram names, at most 50, so the file shows its icons on another phenix server. When the server has no icon of a name, the file does not hold it, and the download says so.

These actions add icons from a file to the server's library:

  • Uploading a file that holds icons.
  • Edit as a draft on the diagram of a topology read from its Builder file.

Builder adds each icon that the server does not have, as uploaded by you. When the server has the same image under that name, Builder discards the copy. The draft keeps its own copy, and Builder says so, in these cases:

  • The server has another image under that name.
  • The server could not take the icon, for example because you reached your upload limit.

The draft shows its copy in place of the server's icon. Add to server in the Custom icons dialog adds a kept copy later. When no node or template of the diagram uses an icon, the icon leaves the diagram with the edit that removed its last use.

Copy and paste include the diagram's copies of the nodes' icons, also into another diagram in the same browser tab.

docs.title: Renaming and deleting icons
docs.text:
Each Builder user can rename and delete each icon that a user uploaded (see The libraries). Rename is in the Custom icons dialog. Delete is on the Icons tab. No user can rename or delete an icon that the server added from a template file (see Template files on the server).

The old name continues to name a renamed icon, so diagrams and templates that use it still show it: "Renamed OLD to NEW. OLD keeps working as another name of it." An icon keeps at most 16 old names. Then the server refuses a new name, and tells you to upload the image under the new name instead. Renaming it back to an old name still works.

Delete asks you to confirm. Diagrams and templates that use the icon, by any of its names, then show their built-in icon. Deleting an icon removes its other names too, and changes no diagram: its nodes keep the name. When another user renamed the icon after Builder read the list, the delete stops. Builder shows the icon as it is now. Check it, and then try again.

docs.title: Several icons at once
docs.text:
In the Custom icons dialog, each diagram copy that the server does not have has a checkbox. Above the copies, a row has Select all, the selected count ("2 of 5 selected") and Add selected to server.

Add selected to server adds each selected copy under its name: "Added 2 icons to the server. The diagram drops its copies with its next edit." When someone added a copy after the dialog opened, the dialog names it: "The server already has plc." You cannot select the server icons in this dialog.

Here, a copy of the pump station diagram gives rtu-01 and eng-ws-01 the icons gauge and tank. The diagram holds these icons and the server does not:

The rows use the keys of the drafts page (see Selecting with the keyboard), with these differences:

  • Escape with nothing selected closes the dialog.
  • In the server icons, the keys only move focus. Delete does nothing.

When some copies could not be added, a summary under the row gives the reason for each. When the server cannot be reached, Builder stops and lists the rest as "Not attempted."

docs.title: Import, Upload and Download: details
docs.text:
Info

This page holds every rule, limit and message of this feature. For the short guide, see Import, Upload and Download.

These pages use three words for these tasks:

  • Import, on the drafts page or the Configs page, makes a draft from a Topology or Experiment config, stored in phenix or in a file. The phenix server converts the config into a diagram.
  • Upload, on the drafts page or in the editor toolbar, opens a file that is already a diagram as a new draft: a Builder document, a Builder package, a published diagram or a legacy Builder diagram.
  • Download, in the editor toolbar, saves the open diagram as a file, in one of seven formats, or as a Builder package.

Import, Download and the upload of a Builder document do not change a config on the phenix server. Only one upload task can write configs: the Create on this server option of a Builder package (see Moving a diagram with a Builder package). Other than that, only Publish writes configs (see Publishing).

To move a diagram, and what it needs, to another phenix server, download a Builder package and upload it there (see Moving a diagram with a Builder package). To show the diagram of a topology kept in files, see A Builder file beside a topology.

The examples on this page use the example lab.

docs.title: Importing a topology or experiment
docs.text: The draft holds what phenix would read from the config. The draft has the name of the source config, or the new topology name for a copy or a combined import.

docs.title: From a stored config
docs.text:
To import the riverside-water topology:

  1. On the drafts page, click Import.
  2. Keep Source set to Stored config and Source kind set to Topology.
  3. In Source name, choose riverside-water. The dialog shows Included topologies, because riverside-water includes corp-services.
  4. Keep the default import options.
  5. Click Import. The dialog shows 1 warning: the 2 nodes from corp-services are read only, and publishing keeps includeTopologies.
  6. Click Continue to editor.

An import without warnings opens the editor immediately. Cancel makes no draft. The open diagram does not change until the editor opens. If you close the dialog while it shows "Importing…", nothing is imported, even when the answer comes later.

In Source name, "(legacy Builder diagram)" marks a topology that the legacy Builder saved. The import converts its diagram. Publishing the draft to the same topology replaces the legacy diagram (see Converting a stored topology).

docs.title: Importing an experiment
docs.text:
To import the riverside experiment:

  1. Click Import.
  2. Set Source kind to Experiment.
  3. In Source name, choose riverside.
  4. Click Import. The dialog shows 2 warnings.
  5. Click Continue to editor.

An imported experiment is different from an imported topology:

  • If your role can list the stored Scenario that the experiment names, the draft lists it. If not, the draft lists no scenario, and the import warns. The import never keeps the copy of the scenario in the experiment, because a diagram names its scenarios and holds none.
  • The VLAN aliases of the experiment become the VLAN alias of each network.
  • The import does not keep the VLAN range, or experiment fields that have no place in a diagram, such as baseDir, defaultBridge and deployMode. A warning names these fields.
  • The import does not keep the files that experiment apps injected into VMs at start, and does not warn about them. It keeps the injections of the topology.
  • The import removes the values that phenix added to the nodes when it created the experiment, so the devices read like topology nodes:
    • Each empty or null field, except a field that a topology must have, such as the interfaces of a network or the vlan of an interface. It removes a 0 or false only when phenix reads it as unset. A field that can be unset, such as snapshot or the cost of a route, keeps an explicit 0 or false.
    • Each value equal to the phenix default, also when the topology set it: vm_type kvm, snapshot true, do_not_boot false, cpu Broadwell, vcpus 1 and memory 512. External nodes keep these values. os_type stays, because a topology must have it.
    • bridge_set_in_topo, and each interface bridge that phenix set to the default bridge of the experiment because the topology set none. Thus a bridge that you change in the draft stays when phenix creates an experiment from the published topology.

docs.title: Importing a config file
docs.text:
